picks.blurb: The Kennesaw State Owls (1-4, 0-1 CUSA) won this league last year and were expected to contend for the title again, but they've had a disappointing start to the year and have dropped back-to-back one-score games. Most recently, they lost 27-26 to Jacksonville State in their league opener. The Missouri State Bears (1-4, 0-1 CUSA), meanwhile, were a surprising bowl team last year in their first season at the FBS level. However, with a new coaching staff this season, they've struggled and are still looking for their first FBS win. Last week, they lost to a Western Kentucky game that looked like it could be the worst in the conference. If you are looking for some betting advice for the matchup, we've got you covered. That offense is a strength relative to the defense, which has been pretty rough overall, particularly against the pass. Missouri State's offense has its own issues, though, and it benched quarterback Skyler Locklear for Henry Belin IV last week. Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 6:44 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 4 Ohio State travels to No. 5 Indiana for a massive Big Noon showdown. Can the Buckeyes avenge last year's Big Ten Championship loss? One of the biggest games of the college football season is set for Saturday afternoon as No. 4 Ohio State travels to Bloomington to take on No. 5 Indiana in FOX's Big Noon Saturday showdown. And there is plenty of bad blood between these two programs. The last time these teams met, Indiana stunned Ohio State 13-10 in the 2025 Big Ten Championship Game, ending the Buckeyes' undefeated season. Now, Ryan Day and Ohio State have an opportunity to return the favor against Curt Cignetti's defending national champions. Ohio State enters at 5-1, while Indiana remains undefeated at 6-0. Both teams are 3-0 in Big Ten play, making this matchup potentially decisive in the conference championship race. Ohio State: Can Julian Sayin Deliver? Ohio State's offense has been explosive this season, averaging more than 42 points per game. Quarterback Julian Sayin has thrown for approximately 1,772 yards, while superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has been nearly unstoppable, recording 48 receptions for 916 yards and 11 touchdowns. Smith is the most dangerous player in college football, and Indiana's secondary will have its hands full trying to contain him. However, last year's championship game exposed some serious problems for Ohio State. Sayin threw for 258 yards, and Smith recorded eight catches for 144 yards, but the Buckeyes managed just 10 points. Sayin was also sacked five times. Indiana's defensive front remains dangerous, averaging 3.3 sacks and 8.2 tackles for loss per game this season. Running back Bo Jackson, who has rushed for approximately 460 yards, must help establish balance and prevent Indiana from focusing entirely on Sayin. Indiana: The Hoosiers Aren't Going Anywhere Indiana might have lost Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza, but Curt Cignetti has kept the Hoosiers rolling. TCU transfer Josh Hoover has thrown for more than 1,300 yards with 17 touchdowns and zero interceptions, while running back Turbo Richard has rushed for nearly 600 yards. Wide receiver Charlie Becker has also been outstanding, recording 529 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. Michigan State transfer Nick Marsh gives Indiana another dangerous weapon on the outside. Defensively, Indiana is allowing approximately 12 points per game and has demonstrated an ability to create pressure without sacrificing coverage. However, the Hoosiers haven't exactly dominated their recent competition. Indiana narrowly escaped Northwestern 29-23 before defeating Nebraska 20-17 last weekend. Those performances raise questions about whether the Hoosiers can consistently move the football against an elite opponent. Expect another physical, defensive battle between two legitimate College Football Playoff contenders. Indiana's defense will create problems for Sayin, and the Hoosiers should find success moving the football through Hoover and Richard. However, Ohio State has something Indiana doesn't: Jeremiah Smith. I expect Smith to deliver a massive performance, surpassing 100 receiving yards and making the difference in a game that comes down to the final possession. Sayin will make a few mistakes under pressure, but the Buckeyes' defense will get enough stops to escape Bloomington with a huge victory. Final Score: No. 4 Ohio State 24, No. 5 Indiana 20 Ohio State gets its revenge, hands Indiana its first loss of the season, and puts itself in an excellent position in the Big Ten championship race. picks.blurb: Cignetti Praises Ohio State as Big Ten Broadcaster Picks Buckeyes Over Indiana - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Packers' Josh Jacobs will be eligible to play Week 7 TRENDING Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Story by Ohio State Buckeyes On SI Cignetti Praises Ohio State as Big Ten Broadcaster Picks Buckeyes Over Indiana Indiana Hoosiers linebacker Isaiah Jones (46) works to bring down Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) on Saturday, Dec. 6, 2025, during the Big Ten football championship at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Landon Buford Thu, October 15, 2026 at 9:41 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This week is another major test for the No. 4 Ohio State Buckeyes, who go on the road to face the No. 5 Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Indiana. During his weekly press conference on Monday, Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti praised Ohio State's talent and coaching staff. "We're playing a great team this week at home in Ohio State. They're a great football team with a lot of great players, and they're extremely well coached. Ryan Day does a great job, and both coordinators and all the position coaches are really, really good," said Cignetti . Cignetti, Day Trade Praise Ahead of Ohio State-Indiana Showdown Later in his press conference, Cignetti talked about facing an Ohio State program that's used to winning championships. "Winning does a lot of good things, and I think that's what's happened. You've got an opponent coming in here that's used to winning and winning championships, and there isn't a stronger brand in America than Ohio State football," Cignetti said . "It's been that way for years and years. We're a team that's still developing, and I'm sure they'd say the same thing about their team. It ought to be a great environment." During his press conference, Buckeyes head coach Ryan Day said this weekend's game against Indiana will be a huge challenge. "It's going to be a huge challenge. They do an excellent job up front on defense," Day said. "Their defensive line is one of the biggest challenges we'll have all season." When asked about Indiana star wide receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh, Day was very complimentary. "These guys in particular are very clean route runners," Day said . "They're really strong on contact, have really good body control, have run-after-the-catch ability. "Certainly, Becker has made some big-time plays in big-time moments, and Marsh is playing as good as anybody right now. This is a huge challenge for our secondary." With both coaches bracing for a tight game, Mark Followill shared his pick with Ohio State Buckeyes on SI . Mark Followill Picks Ohio State in a Near Coin Flip In an exclusive interview, Mark Followill, the TV play-by-play voice of the Dallas Mavericks and a Big Ten Network broadcaster who called Ohio State's win over Maryland last weekend, gave his prediction for Saturday's top-five showdown and explained why he's leaning toward the Buckeyes. "To me, this is a very even matchup. But when in doubt, because of what I've seen in person and what I saw of his performances in the lead-up to the game, I'm going to lean toward the team that's got the best player on the field," Followill said. "I don't want to say he can win the game single-handedly, but if the game is in the balance, he's more likely than anyone else to make a game-tipping play." He went on to say that he likes Indiana's team as well, but Ohio State's playmakers make it difficult to sway his opinion on where the result will go. "I like Indiana's defense a lot. They can pressure the passer without having to sell out to do it. But Ohio State is showing me that, on top of having an explosive playmaker in Jeremiah Smith who can pop off a big play at any time, they can dominate the line of scrimmage and the run game even when their offensive line isn't at full strength," Followill said. "If you've got that, I'm going to roll with them.. "I think it's going to be a fantastic freaking game. If you're going to pin me down and force me to make a prediction, that's the way I'm going to lean. I'll give you 52-48 percentage." The Buckeyes and Hoosiers kick off Saturday at 12 pm EDT at Memorial Stadium, with the game airing on FOX. away.headline: Ohio State football releases first injury report vs. Indiana: Who’s in, who’s out for the Buckeyes
away.blurb: Offensive lineman Austin Siereveld, who missed last week’s win against Maryland, was deemed out on Wednesday’s injury report — the first of four reports this week. Running back Ja’Kobi Jackson, who has appeared in every game for the Buckeyes this season, was also listed as out. He has started the last two games for Ohio State, though running back Bo Jackson had more carries in both contests. Receiver Brock Boyd, running back Isaiah West, defensive end Khary Wilder and offensive lineman Deontae Armstrong were listed as questionable. Linebacker Christian Alliegro, defensive back Jay Timmons, offensive tackle Phillip Daniels and receivers Devin McCuin and Brandon Inniss were not on the report, suggesting they’ll be available after missing last week’s win vs. Maryland. While Timmons could return this week, safety Leroy Roker — who has also been sidelined since Sept. 26 — was listed as out. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State plays at Indiana on Saturday in one of the biggest games of the college football regular season. away.headline: Ohio State football got some injury news it badly needed ahead of Saturday's game vs. Indiana
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The Ohio State Buckeyes received rough news Wednesday when the initial availability report listed offensive lineman Austin Siereveld and running back Ja'Kobi Jackson as out against Indiana . Another worry on that first report was running back Isaiah West, who was listed as questionable. With Ja'Kobi Jackson already ruled out, Legend Bey looked like he would have to serve as Ohio State’s second running back behind starter Bo Jackson. Thursday night’s availability report brought good news for the Buckeyes. West, freshman defensive end Khary Wilder, and backup offensive lineman Deontae Armstrong were all listed as questionable Wednesday. All three have since been removed from the report and are expected to play against Indiana. West’s status is the one that's getting the attention here. He has 22 carries for 80 rushing yards and one touchdown. With Ja'Kobi Jackson out, West will be Ohio State’s second running back in this game. He’ll need to be ready to handle a real share of the carries against a strong Indiana defensive front. Keeping Bo Jackson fresh is going to be key in a game of this size. Having West available gives Ohio State a second back instead of pushing a deeper option into a bigger role on the road. Wide receiver Brock Boyd is the only other notable Buckeye still listed as questionable to play against Indiana. On the flip side, Ohio State will have five starters back who didn’t play a week ago against Maryland. Wide receivers Brandon Inniss and Devin McCuin, cornerback Jay Timmons, linebacker Christian Alliegro, and offensive lineman Phillip Daniels will all return against the Hoosiers. That’s a significant boost across the lineup. Inniss and McCuin give the passing game two more targets, and Timmons and Alliegro return to a defense that will face one of its toughest tests yet. Daniels coming back also helps an offensive line that will be without Siereveld. Midweek wasn't great at all for Ohio State on the injury front, but the latest news did bring welcomed news for the Buckeyes. Ohio State is heading into a top-5 matchup with the Hoosiers that will shape the Big Ten race at the end of the season. The Buckeyes need to be as healthy as possible for it. Isaiah West cleared to play against Indiana Ohio State gets 5 starters back from the Maryland game Siereveld and Ja'Kobi Jackson are still the two notable absences for Ohio State heading into Bloomington. Losing a starting offensive lineman and a running back at the same time puts more pressure on the run game against a defense that has been tough up front. Still, getting West off the availability report is welcome news for the Buckeyes. Ohio State is going to need its run game Saturday in Bloomington, and the backfield now has more depth than it appeared to have Wednesday. How the Buckeyes split the carries between Bo Jackson and West against Indiana’s front will be worth watching. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. home.blurb: Offensive lineman Austin Siereveld, who missed last week’s win against Maryland, was deemed out on Wednesday’s injury report — the first of four reports this week. Running back Ja’Kobi Jackson, who has appeared in every game for the Buckeyes this season, was also listed as out. He has started the last two games for Ohio State, though running back Bo Jackson had more carries in both contests. Receiver Brock Boyd, running back Isaiah West, defensive end Khary Wilder and offensive lineman Deontae Armstrong were listed as questionable. Linebacker Christian Alliegro, defensive back Jay Timmons, offensive tackle Phillip Daniels and receivers Devin McCuin and Brandon Inniss were not on the report, suggesting they’ll be available after missing last week’s win vs. Maryland. While Timmons could return this week, safety Leroy Roker — who has also been sidelined since Sept. 26 — was listed as out. COLUMBUS, Ohio — Ohio State plays at Indiana on Saturday in one of the biggest games of the college football regular season. However, the Buckeyes won’t be at full strength for the matchup. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

home.headline: Ohio State football got some injury news it badly needed ahead of Saturday's game vs. Indiana
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: The Ohio State Buckeyes received rough news Wednesday when the initial availability report listed offensive lineman Austin Siereveld and running back Ja'Kobi Jackson as out against Indiana . Another worry on that first report was running back Isaiah West, who was listed as questionable. With Ja'Kobi Jackson already ruled out, Legend Bey looked like he would have to serve as Ohio State’s second running back behind starter Bo Jackson. Thursday night’s availability report brought good news for the Buckeyes. West, freshman defensive end Khary Wilder, and backup offensive lineman Deontae Armstrong were all listed as questionable Wednesday. All three have since been removed from the report and are expected to play against Indiana. West’s status is the one that's getting the attention here. He has 22 carries for 80 rushing yards and one touchdown. With Ja'Kobi Jackson out, West will be Ohio State’s second running back in this game. He’ll need to be ready to handle a real share of the carries against a strong Indiana defensive front. Keeping Bo Jackson fresh is going to be key in a game of this size. Having West available gives Ohio State a second back instead of pushing a deeper option into a bigger role on the road. Wide receiver Brock Boyd is the only other notable Buckeye still listed as questionable to play against Indiana. On the flip side, Ohio State will have five starters back who didn’t play a week ago against Maryland. Wide receivers Brandon Inniss and Devin McCuin, cornerback Jay Timmons, linebacker Christian Alliegro, and offensive lineman Phillip Daniels will all return against the Hoosiers. That’s a significant boost across the lineup. Inniss and McCuin give the passing game two more targets, and Timmons and Alliegro return to a defense that will face one of its toughest tests yet. Daniels coming back also helps an offensive line that will be without Siereveld. Midweek wasn't great at all for Ohio State on the injury front, but the latest news did bring welcomed news for the Buckeyes. Ohio State is heading into a top-5 matchup with the Hoosiers that will shape the Big Ten race at the end of the season. The Buckeyes need to be as healthy as possible for it. Isaiah West cleared to play against Indiana Ohio State gets 5 starters back from the Maryland game Siereveld and Ja'Kobi Jackson are still the two notable absences for Ohio State heading into Bloomington. Losing a starting offensive lineman and a running back at the same time puts more pressure on the run game against a defense that has been tough up front. Still, getting West off the availability report is welcome news for the Buckeyes. Ohio State is going to need its run game Saturday in Bloomington, and the backfield now has more depth than it appeared to have Wednesday. How the Buckeyes split the carries between Bo Jackson and West against Indiana’s front will be worth watching. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. home.blurb: With a battle in Bloomington with defending champs Indiana this coming weekend, Day claimed that some of the players who were held out of Week 6 will be suited up and ready to go in Week 7. If Inniss and McCuin are out, Jeremiah Smith should be able to keep the offense afloat. The only way that happens is if Siereveld is back in the interior and Daniels reprises his role at right tackle. Neither graded out particularly well early, but the line has its most consistency from the offseason with both back on the right side. Having either miss the Indiana game would be a disaster. Particularly Timmons, who has Davion Chandler as a major weapon out of the slot. Outside receivers like Nick Marsh and Charlie Becker will give the Buckeyes hell, but being without Timmons opens up even more avenues for Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover in the passing game. home.headline: Ohio State football at Indiana updates, injuries, storylines
home.blurb: Rob Oller, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 27, Indiana 17 : Considering I predicted two regular-season losses for the Buckeyes, this would be a natural game to have OSU taking a loss, but while it should be a tough Memorial Stadium environment (for a change), I just don't see the Hoosiers doing enough to stun the Buckeyes for a second consecutive season. Indiana coach Curt Cignetti may well be a magician, but IU won't pull a win out of its hat. Ohio State's defensive line, a weak point to begin the season, is rounding into form at just the right time, and the Buckeyes' run game will do just enough to keep IU honest, allowing the Julian Sayin-Jeremiah Smith connection to keep going strong. The return of Stephen Daley, who received a fifth year of eligibility following a court ruling, has bolstered a stout defensive line. The Hoosiers’ 20 sacks are the third-most in the FBS, including five in five games from Daley. home.blurb: Ryan Day made a noteworthy admission on the injury front after Ohio State beat Maryland that stands out for the Indiana game Skip to content Coming out of this one, a lot of the chatter is going to center on the injury front . Ohio State has a big Week 7 game against the Indiana Hoosiers in Bloomington, and who the Buckeyes get back will matter. Siereveld wasn't the only one out. Ohio State was also without linebacker Christian Alliegro, cornerback Jay Timmons, wide receivers Brandon Inniss and Devin McCuin, offensive lineman Phillip Daniels, and defensive end Khary Wilder against the Terrapins. Part of that comes down to game flow. Ohio State leaned on the run more than usual and attempted just 21 passes. Even so, not having Inniss and McCuin available was notable. Smith can carry a passing game for stretches, but the Buckeyes need secondary options to keep defenses honest, and Indiana will be a much tougher test than Maryland. The injury front is going to be a topic of discussion all week ahead of the trip to Indiana. Ohio State expects a good portion of the injury list back, but which names return will shape how this Week 7 matchup plays out. The Buckeyes have a lot on the injury front to work through in the next week. The Ohio State Buckeyes moved to 5-1 with a 45-16 win over the Maryland Terrapins on Saturday. It wasn't a perfect performance. Ohio State had several miscues, including turnovers, and left plenty of room to play better. Still, the Buckeyes scored in every quarter and held Maryland to 146 total yards while racking up 449 yards of offense. Ohio State was missing several starters against Maryland Ohio State didn't learn until hours before kickoff that offensive lineman Austin Siereveld would miss the game against Maryland. Siereveld is dealing with a non-football injury. Ryan Day isn't going to share what happened, and that's understandable. He's a player worth monitoring to see whether he can suit up against Indiana. With Indiana up next, you'd like to see Ohio State get all of those players back, especially with the majority of them being starters. It was all but confirmed after the game that probably won't be the case. “I don't think we'll get all of those guys back that were on the list, but for sure we're going to get you know a good portion of them back for next week,” Day said . “So that'll be good. Manning's inconsistency has kept the Longhorns' offense largely out of rhythm this season, a critique he'll try to correct against the SEC's worst defense. After a loss to rival Oklahoma sent the Longhorns falling six spots in the AP Poll, Texas is hoping to use the tailspinning Gators as their punching bag to stay in the College Football Playoff picture. The Gators struggled to block Gamecocks edge Dylan Stewart and now must endure the athleticism of Colin Simmons , who leads college football with 9.5 sacks. Simmons collected five sacks during a win at Tennessee last month and is the runaway favorite to win the SEC's Defensive Player of the Year honor. Texas vs. Florida: Need to know Turnovers and touchdowns: Manning's production against Power Four competition has been pedestrian -- four touchdown passes and four interceptions. Two came during the fourth quarter of last week's loss to Oklahoma, including a pick-six that swung the game's momentum to the Sooners. Manning's been sacked 12 times through five games -- 10 coming against Ohio State , Tennessee and Oklahoma. If there's a get-right opportunity for Florida's defense, perhaps this is it. Frightening defensive numbers: Florida ranks last in the SEC in total defense, explosive plays allowed, pass defense and 15th in scoring defense this season. Sumrall said this week he was taking a closer look at multiple areas of his team to try and fix what has nuked this 4-0 start for the Gators. It starts with getting stops on defense against the Longhorns. Longhorns' second 'revenge' game: A failure-to-show loss against the Gators in Gainesville ultimately kept Texas out of the CFP last year. Now, Sarkisian's squad has a chance to move to 2-0 this season in revenge opportunities after beating Ohio State in Week 2. Texas remains in this week's updated CFP projection with a first-round home game and has a clear-cut path to the 12-team bracket, but Saturday's a must-win. However, since that high-water mark, things have looked grim for the Orange and Blue after getting outscored 83-35 in its two losses to Missouri and South Carolina. As for the Longhorns, they also began the fall campaign with four straight wins — a streak that included a 24-23 triumph over then-No. 1 Ohio State. With a second straight loss to the Gators, Texas would be on the verge of losing any hopes of a spot in the College Football Playoff . But a victory would right the ship for the Longhorns, especially if beleaguered quarterback Arch Manning and an error-prone special teams can trim the mistakes and play a clean game. Under first-year coach Jon Sumrall and breakout running back Jadan Baugh , Florida became one of the early-season darlings of college football after knocking off Ole Miss and climbing into the top 10 of the AP rankings. But the Gators have fallen out of the poll following two straight losses, and a porous Florida defense has given up a combined 83 points over the past two weeks to Missouri and South Carolina. Here's a full scouting report for the Texas Longhorns vs. the Florida Gators. No. 7 Texas (4-1, 1-1 SEC) vs. Florida (4-2, 2-2) When: 11 a.m. Saturday Where: Royal-Memorial Stadium TV/radio: ABC, 1300, 98.1, 105.3 (Spanish) Weather: Finally, football weather. A Friday cold front drops the temperatures near 50 degrees at kickoff and won't rise much above 70. There may be a few clouds but not much chance of rain. The Longhorns held on to the tie by stopping heralded Gator fullback Bill Middlekauff four times inside their own 3-yard line in the final minute of the game. MORE: 'Everything we want is is still right in front of us': Texas football eyes glimmer of hope MORE: Gators QB Aaron Philo uncertain to play due to reported injury Know the foe: Florida Last week: Lost to South Carolina, 38-19 Players to watch: RB Jadan Baugh , a 6-foot-1, 225-pound junior, serves as the centerpiece of the Gator offense. He ranks third in the SEC with 672 yards rushing and leads the conference with 12 rushing touchdowns. In two games against Texas over the past two seasons, he racked up 195 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. QB Aaron Philo , a 6-1, 207-pound junior transfer from Georgia Tech, has been solid if not spectacular, but he may miss the Texas game with an injury . He's thrown for 1,341 yards on 70.5% passing with nine touchdowns and three interceptions and has added 104 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Edge Jayden Woods, a 6-3, 245-pound sophomore, may not quite be at the level of Texas All-American edge Colin Simmons, but he's getting closer. The twitchy pass rusher has 4 ½ sacks and six tackles for a loss, and he'll test the Longhorn pass protection. Over the past two games against Missouri's Austin Simmons and South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers, Florida's pass defense has allowed a combined 619 yards on 70.8% passing with six touchdown passes and no interceptions. Those two quarterbacks averaged 13.5 yards per completion against the Gators, which could mean lots of action downfield for Texas receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo . Will freshman Derrek Cooper get more snaps at running back for Texas? He showed flashes with a team-high 41 yards rushing against Oklahoma but averages just 3.5 yards per carry for the season. That's even lower than the Longhorns' paltry team average of 3.7 yards a carry. Buoyed by linebacker Myles Graham (41 tackles), the Gators have been respectable against the run while allowing 124.3 yards a game and 3.9 yards a carry. When Florida has the ball Florida won't shy away from the run. It ranks fifth in the SEC with 200.3 yards rushing a game and averages more than 5 yards a carry as a team. Baugh carries the load, but dynamic Duke Clark (265 yards rushing, 7.4 yards per carry) provides an intriguing change of pace. Texas allows just 96 yards rushing a game and 2.8 yards a carry, but linebackers Rasheem Biles (42 tackles) and Justin Cryer (27) are most effective using their speed to chase down backs instead of having to take on linemen. Texas outside corners Bo Mascoe and Kade Phillips have had issues this season, especially when it comes to drawing flags. Florida could test that pair as well as the rest of the secondary if healthy, but that's a big question mark entering Saturday's game. Dallas Wilson (26 catches, 376 yards, three touchdowns) had a breakout game against Texas last season. However, fellow wideout Vernell Brown III has missed the past two games with a knee injury. Brown has 17 receptions for 271 yards and two touchdowns in four games and has also returned two punts for a touchdown. If Robertson and guards Dylan Sikorski and Brandon Baker can't clear some running lanes against Bett and the Gators, they may never get the ground game going. picks.blurb: Florida vs. Texas Final Score Predictions: Experts weigh in on a desperate Gators team heading to Austin - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Packers' Josh Jacobs will be eligible to play Week 7 TRENDING Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Alan Youngblood/Gainesville Sun-Imagn Images, Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images Brandon Little, Craig Smith, Justin Churchill, Rob Gregson, Ryan Roberts, Tyler Forness Thu, October 15, 2026 at 6:48 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After suffering back-to-back embarrassing losses, can the Florida Gators get back in the win column against a reeling Texas Longhorns team? The Florida Gators are in a rough spot at 4-2 as they head to Austin to take on the Texas Longhorns on Saturday afternoon. After two blowout losses to the Missouri Tigers and South Carolina Gamecocks on homecoming, Jon Sumrall 's team is in a tough spot. They were at one point being talked about as potentially being the 2019 LSU Tigers from on the precipice of collapsing. It's his first year at the helm, and the talent level still isn't quite there yet. For the Longhorns, they have beaten Ohio State, but are coming off a tough loss in the Red River Rivalry to the Oklahoma Sooners. They are in an interesting spot right now, and a win is a must for both teams. Who will get the win? Our experts made their predictions. Texas 38, Florida 24 Can we trust the Florida Gators? Honestly, no, and that includes the four-game winning streak to start the season with a massive blowout win over Ole Miss. The defense is struggling to generate pressure and the coverage on the back end has been incredibly inconsistent. Even with Texas having lost Red River last week, their success so far this season and offensive talent gets the Longhorns the win. Can the Gators get the win? Absolutely! Will they? I doubt it. – Tyler Forness , A to Z Florida Texas 33, Florida 19 Both teams come in off dismal losses to unranked teams. The Longhorns, who haven't looked dominant this year by any means, gagged away a game they should have won against Oklahoma but for a pick six and a punt block touchdown. Florida got mollywhopped by South Carolina one game after getting throttled by Missouri. As such, it's tough to tell up from down with these two teams. But my mind immediately goes to two things. First, the Horns' front is still nasty, and Florida suddenly can't find any space for Jadan Baugh and the ground game. On the other side, Florida's defense has become a sieve, and I don't trust they've found a way to fix it yet. Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo are too much for the Longhorns, who win comfortably in Austin. – Craig Smith , A to Z Miami Texas 31, Florida 20 Arch Manning has faced plenty of criticism for his inconsistency this season, but this is the type of matchup that could help him get back on track. Florida's pass defense has been a major weakness, and I expect Manning to take full advantage by delivering his best performance of the 2026 season. The Longhorns have the talent to exploit the Gators' struggling secondary, and Manning should find plenty of opportunities to push the ball downfield and put points on the board. After an uneven stretch offensively, this could be the breakthrough performance Texas needs. Florida should have some success early, particularly with running back Jadan Baugh leading the way. Baugh has been one of the Gators' most productive playmakers, and I expect him to help Florida move the ball and keep the game competitive in the first half. However, Texas has the defensive talent to make adjustments and limit Florida's offensive production as the game progresses. The Gators have struggled to maintain consistency in recent weeks, and that issue will catch up with them again in Austin. Texas pulls away in the second half, with Manning and the offense doing enough to secure a much-needed win. – Ryan Roberts , A to Z Notre Dame Texas 21, Florida 17 The Gators have fallen off a bit in the last few weeks after starting red hot. Texas is coming off a disappointing loss to Oklahoma. So, you know, Steve Sarkisian is going to be looking to get his team rolling again. Last week probably showed Texas what they should be doing more often on offense. They need to run more quick-game stuff with Arch Manning, because the long, developing routes downfield aren't helping the offense. Their offensive line isn't great, so they need to start running more quick-game plays. I think this past game showed some of that, and Texas still gets the win despite the offense struggling against a decent Florida defense. – Justin Churchill , A to Z Oklahoma Texas 30, Florida 20 As high as I was on the Florida Gators after the Ole Miss win, that hype has come crashing down after games against Missouri and South Carolina. The offense, led by Jadan Baugh, simply hasn't looked the same, and now the availability of starting QB Aaron Philo is in question. As for Texas, the Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing loss of their own after losing Red River to a bad OU team, and they aim to get back on track. Florida's defense has been bad, to say the least, and this game may serve as a great game for Arch Manning nd Texas. Give me the Longhorns here. – Rob Gregson , A to Z Alabama Texas 28, Florida 17 Texas and Florida both need wins this week, and the pressure is even higher for Steve Sarkisian and Arch Manning. Texas' second half collapse in the Red River Shootout last weekend has reverberated throughout college football. If Jones does get the start, he’ll likely have star wide receiver Vernell Brown III available after practicing on Wednesday. Brown hasn’t played in the last two games. According to Inside Texas , Terry practiced on Wednesday and is expected to be available on Saturday. home.blurb: And they've done it without having defensive lineman Justus Terry for the past three games. He suffered a foot/turf toe injury during warmups against Ohio State, forcing him out of that contest and the next two games against UTSA and Tennessee. Wearing a walking boot, he's had to watch from the sidelines. On the initial injury report for Texas' matchup with Oklahoma on Saturday, Terry was listed as doubtful but was upgraded to questionable leading into the weekend. He was then upgraded to a game-time decision on Saturday morning. The Texas Longhorns have proved early this season that they have one of the best defenses in the country. Terry suited up for pregame warmups before kickoff against Oklahoma. However, fans were left with more questions than answers once the game started. Justus Terry Suited Up But Appears Inactive vs. Oklahoma Terry remained suited up once the game started but he didn't play in the first half against the Sooners. On multiple defensive possessions, he was seen on the sideline without his helmet, not a good sign for his availability. Perhaps Texas plans to use him as an emergency option on the defensive line if other players were to go down with injury. It appears Terry is still a week away from playing notable snaps again. The Longhorns host Florida next weekend. This is a breaking news article that will be updated accordingly. LSU 48, Mississippi State 24 Brooke Benedict Unlike last weekend's loss to Kentucky, LSU has to get both sides of the ball to play all four quarters, with the defense able to shut down Mississippi State's pass threat, and Sam Leavitt and his receiver options are able to make key plays during possessions. Without any system errors from the offense, defense and special teams, the team will see some much-needed success back at home, being able to win over the Bulldogs and win back their top-ranked reputation. LSU 33, Mississippi State 21 If Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor plays: Kamario Taylor has an incredible ability to control the long ball, which will force LSU's defense to account for that threat almost all of the time, and following the loss to Kentucky, I expect LSU to play a lot more tight man coverage. The LSU offense, clearly more comfortable playing at home, will establish the run with Dilin Jones against the MSST 3-3-5 defense, and LSU will win a close one late in the 4th. LSU 38, Mississippi State 31 If Taylor doesn't play: If Taylor is unavailable in Saturday's game, the MSST backup QB is not a clear answer. Redshirt Freshman Parker Puckett started in place of Taylor against Alabama, but SEC veteran AJ Swann is also a likely option to play. Regardless, I expect the Bulldogs will be less competitive without the SEC TD leader hurling the rock. LSU wins handily at home. Taylor is one of college football’s best quarterbacks, and if he’s not healthy, LSU’s defensive game plan changes. The pressure is mounting in Baton Rouge as No. 22 LSU (4-2) prepares to host No. 16 Mississippi State (4-2) Saturday afternoon at Tiger Stadium. Lane Kiffin's Tigers are coming off an embarrassing 35-34 overtime loss to Kentucky, a game LSU had every opportunity to win before a questionable fourth-down decision allowed the Wildcats to force overtime. Meanwhile, Mississippi State is looking to bounce back after a disappointing loss to Alabama. With LSU already sitting at 1-2 in SEC play, another conference loss could effectively end the Tigers' College Football Playoff hopes. LSU: Can Sam Leavitt Save the Tigers? LSU's offense has shown flashes of brilliance under Kiffin, but consistency remains a major concern. Quarterback Sam Leavitt has thrown for 1,495 yards and 10 touchdowns, but his eight interceptions are the most of any quarterback in the SEC. Those turnovers have been a major issue for a team that possesses enough offensive talent to compete with nearly anyone. Running back Dilin Jones has provided stability in the backfield, rushing for 426 yards and five touchdowns through LSU's first five games. Wide receiver Winston Watkins Jr. has also emerged as a dangerous weapon, recording 354 receiving yards. Defensively, LSU has been impressive at times, particularly with edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, who recorded eight sacks through the team's first five games. However, the Tigers just surrendered 35 points to Kentucky, raising serious questions about their ability to close out games. Against Mississippi State's explosive offense, LSU cannot afford another inconsistent defensive performance. Mississippi State: Kamario Taylor Is a PROBLEM Jeff Lebby has Mississippi State playing some exciting football, and quarterback Kamario Taylor has emerged as one of the SEC's most dangerous young players. Taylor has thrown for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns, and just four interceptions while completing 66.2% of his passes. However, his availability is a major concern after aggravating a lower-leg injury against Alabama. If Taylor is healthy enough to play, LSU's defense will have its hands full. Wide receiver Anthony Evans III has been outstanding, recording 40 receptions for 574 yards and five touchdowns through five games. Running back Fluff Bothwell has also been productive, rushing for 403 yards and three touchdowns while averaging 5.4 yards per carry. The Bulldogs possess enough offensive firepower to challenge LSU, but their defense remains vulnerable. Mississippi State was allowing 28 points and nearly 380 yards per game through its first five contests. That's a dangerous weakness against a Kiffin-led offense playing at home. Establishing Jones early should also create opportunities for explosive passing plays. Defensively, LSU needs to pressure Taylor if he plays and prevent Evans from creating big plays downfield. For Mississippi State, the formula revolves around attacking LSU's defense with tempo and forcing Leavitt into mistakes. If Taylor is available, his dual-threat ability could create serious problems. The Bulldogs must also establish Bothwell to prevent LSU from focusing entirely on the passing game. I expect an offensive shootout in Baton Rouge. Mississippi State has enough offensive talent to create problems for LSU, particularly if Taylor is healthy enough to play. However, I believe this is a bounce-back opportunity for Kiffin and the Tigers. Leavitt should have success attacking Mississippi State's secondary, and I expect him to throw for more than 300 yards and three touchdowns. The Bulldogs will keep things competitive throughout the afternoon, but LSU's home-field advantage and offensive firepower should ultimately make the difference. Expect Mississippi State to threaten late before LSU's defense comes up with a crucial stop to secure the victory. Lane Kiffin and his Tigers (4-2, 1-2 SEC) have suffered two losses by the midway point of the 2026 regular season, a position where no team has earned an at-large berth into the expanded, 12-team College Football Playoff field. That doesn't mean the door is 100% closed, but No. 21 LSU now has zero room for error. That feels to be a very tricky spot to be in with longtime rival No. 19 Mississippi State (4-1, 2-1) and quarterback Kamario Taylor coming to Baton Rouge for an 11 a.m. CT kickoff Saturday, Oct. 17 on ESPN. LANE KIFFIN ON KAMARIO TAYLOR Lane Kiffin calls Mississippi State QB Kamario Taylor 'a problem' SAM LEAVITT VS KENTUCKY LSU football QB Sam Leavitt said turnovers hurt Tigers vs Kentucky LSU is coming off a heartbreaking overtime loss at Kentucky, 35-34. The Bulldogs rested last week with an off week. Here's what to know about the LSU-Mississippi State pivotal SEC showdown. Mandatory Credit: Jordan Prather-Imagn Images (Jordan Prather, IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) 1 / 15 LSU football at Kentucky: Game photos from the sidelines LSU football at Kentucky: Game photos from the sidelines Kamario Taylor's health Kiffin called the Bulldogs' sophomore quarterback a "problem" earlier this week. Kiffin's Ole Miss squad saw Taylor in the regular season finale last year and he and current Ole Miss head coach, then defensive coordinator Pete Golding may still be having visions of Taylor gashing the defense. In that game, Taylor ran for 173 yards and two touchdowns. He nearly rushed for more yards than he threw for; he had 178 passing yards. Ole Miss won the game comfortably, 38-19, but as Kiffin said, Taylor has all the tools to be very problematic for defenses. Mississippi State wasn't able to firmly challenge Alabama at home two weeks ago before the off week. Taylor threw a couple of interceptions and fumbled the ball. So, turnovers were a major issues, but the dual-threat quarterback was also limited in what he could as he's been contending with a lower leg injury. It remains to be seen how healthy Taylor will be, but if he's close to 100%, or fully healthy, this game could be very interesting. Sam Leavitt turnover issues getting perfect matchup? All season to this point, LSU junior starting quarterback Sam Leavitt has had turnover problems. He's the only quarterback in college football that has thrown an interception in every game this year and his eight picks lead FBS. It's a very troubling stat and, if that trend continues, more losses are on the way for the Tigers. But is the Mississippi State defense the perfect matchup for Leavitt? Are the Bulldogs just what the doctor ordered for LSU's gunslinger? So far this season, the Bulldogs have two interceptions and their pass defense is among the worst in the SEC. Mississippi State has also only recovered two fumbles. Good news for Leavitt is Mississippi State doesn't force turnovers. Early kickoff makes LSU's matchup with Mississippi State scarier? The earliest LSU has kicked off a game in the first half of the regular season was 6 p.m. CT. And that was last week. Does that make this 11 a.m. kickoff spot scary for the Tigers welcoming in Mississippi State? The Bulldogs have only played one game so far at 11 a.m., the loss to Alabama. But it also had a 2:30 p.m. kickoff at Minnesota, which they won, 38-13. LSU practiced in the mornings during fall camp and in season. So, to Kiffin, there shouldn't been an adjustment for his team. "I think we'll play really well," Kiffin said earlier this week. "We practice in the morning every day. So they're up doing that. It's really more what their clock is. I used to be more concerned when we went to this format of the night games being opposite of their body clock. So I don't see it being an issue." LSU football offensive line play LSU struggled to find traditional balance on offense at Kentucky last week. The Wildcats don't have an awesome rush defense, but were able to keep Tiger running backs Dilin Jones and Harlem Berry from getting much of anything going. They combined for 60 rushing yards. Mississippi State's rush defense has fared better so far this season than Kentucky's has, allowing almost 16 yards on the ground less. The Bulldogs have given up five rushing scores on the season. The play up front from LSU's offense must be better this week for the team to keep the Bulldogs at bay. LSU sports the third best running attack in the SEC at 213 yards per game, but Leavitt has played a large role in that and he leads the team in rushing scores with seven. LSU's offensive line need to open run lanes for Jones and Berry against Mississippi State. LSU vs Mississippi State prediction The last time LSU lost under Kiffin a few weeks ago, it was able to bounce back at home and take care of business. Quarterback Kamario Taylor in head coach Jeff Lebby's high-flying offense poses a legit threat to any defense. And this game being an 11 a.m. kickoff also feels like a prime disaster spot for the Tigers. This game will be high scoring, but the question is: which defense will find enough stops to seal the win? I think LSU gets a couple more stops than Mississippi State's defense that averages giving up almost 40 points a game in SEC play. away.headline: Kamario Taylor injury update: Mississippi State QB questionable vs LSU
away.blurb: Taylor was listed on Mississippi State's initial SEC availability report Wednesday as questionable for Saturday's showdown against the 21st-ranked Tigers as he continues to deal with an undisclosed lower-leg injury. Taylor was listed as questionable on Mississippi State's initial SEC player availability report on Wednesday for Saturday's game vs. LSU. Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify . Whether the Bulldogs will have starting quarterback Kamario Taylor under center remains uncertain. The 6-foot-4 quarterback has been one of the breakout players in the SEC through the first six weeks of the season, as he is tied for the third-most touchdown passes in the country (17) and leads the SEC with 290.0 passing yards per game. The hot start for Taylor took a bit of a halt in Week 5 vs. Alabama, as he completed a season-low 55.9% of his passes for 258 yards and three touchdowns while taking five sacks and throwing for two interceptions. Mississippi State and LSU are set for a noon ET kickoff at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge on Saturday, Oct. 17. Here's the latest on Taylor's injury: Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby offered little clarity on the Bulldogs' quarterback situation Monday, keeping details brief when asked about the position ahead of this week's game against LSU. "Right now, the focus is getting (Taylor) ready to play and then having the ability to continue to create the depth in the room," Lebby said on Monday. "Billy (Puckett) and AJ (Swann) obviously are the two guys that have been competing since Day 1 in fall camp and really last spring. So, those guys obviously have the ability to get work if (Taylor) wasn't ready to roll." picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Georgia Football's Clash with Auburn on Saturday Skip to main content SI.COM SI.COM BULLDOGS FB SI.COM BULLDOGS BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Georgia Bulldogs will face off against the Auburn Tigers in the Deep South’s Oldest Rivalry on Saturday afternoon. The weather forecast calls for a beautiful fall Saturday, where the high in Athens is supposed to be just 67 degrees. The betting forecast is calling for the Dawgs to beat the Tigers by about three touchdowns. This will likely not be a close game, which means we can be a little looser with our bold predictions for it. Here are three bold ones for Kirby Smart and Alex Golesh’s first game in this rivalry: Georgia has a 100-Yard Rusher and Receiver The Dawgs can take advantage of this Auburn defense, which is a bottom half unit in the conference, allowing over 350 yards of total offense per game. Georgia’s offense has been extremely productive, ranking top three in the conference. Georgia having a back and a wideout go for 100 yards in the same game hasn’t happened in 10 years. So, yeah. This is a bold prediction. I think about a guy like Talyn Taylor or Craig Dandridge, who have hit on some explosive passing plays. All it takes is one or two of those and some screens and underneath throws to work for that 100-yard game to come into play. Auburn is also among the worst rushing defenses in the SEC. We saw Dwight Phillips Jr. run for over 100 yards against Alabama on just 17 carries. He, Nate Frazier and Bo Walker have each registered multiple explosive runs. All it takes is for one of them to bust a huge run and that 100-yard mark is well within reach. Dawgs go for 250 On the Ground Auburn is allowing about 150 yards per game on the ground. I think Georgia could go for over 250. They have done it twice already and ran for over 200 yards in two other games. Auburn allowed almost 250 yards to both Tennessee and Florida. Georgia has a better offense than both of those teams. The Dawgs could really blow Auburn out on Saturday, and if they do that then there will be a lot of yards gained on the ground. Partially due to garbage time. Georgia Holds Auburn to Under 300 Total Yards Auburn has possibly the most unique offense that Georgia will see all year. There is an argument to be made that the Dawgs will struggle more in this game than you would initially think because of that. Auburn takes the least amount of time in between plays and runs more options and designed quarterback run plays than any other offense that Georgia will see this year. I am not buying it. Georgia’s defense has been the best in college football. The Dawgs will shut down Auburn on Saturday. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. Georgia just got by Alabama in a controversial 20-17 thriller – let's just say the Bulldogs got a wee bit of a break on a key Crimson Tide deep shot – and now it's the No. 1 team in the country. Auburn has had two weeks off to get ready for this, and knocking the Bulldogs off of their lofty perch would put the first season under head coach Alex Golesh into hyperdrive. home.headline: Auburn vs. Georgia early injury report: Who's in, who's out
home.blurb: The Tigers emerge from the bye week relatively healthy, with only two players, tight end Hunter Herring and offensive lineman Tai Buster, ruled out for Saturday's game at Georgia due to injury. However, the biggest news from the initial report is that linebacker Xavier Atkins is officially ruled out. Auburn Tigers — OUT: LB Xavier Atkins, TE Hunter Herring, OL Tai Buster Georgia Bulldogs — OUT: WR Thomas Blackshear, RB Chauncey Bowens, WR Isiah Canion, LB Amaris Williams, S Tyriq Green; Questionable: DB KJ Bolden; Probable: OL Marcus Harrison Atkins, who is tied for the team lead in sacks and second on the team in tackles, has been suspended for Saturday's game at No. 1 Georgia, according to Auburn head coach Alex Golesh. Golesh first mentioned the suspension during Monday's press conference and clarified Wednesday that Atkins is not with the team during practice this week. Golesh will address Atkins' status again next week. The Bulldogs will be without several players, including running back Chauncey Bowens, who leads the team in rushing touchdowns with six. However, Georgia received potentially good news on Wednesday as running back Nate Frazier is not on the availability report after missing four straight games with a rib injury. He was not included on the availability report for Georgia's Week 6 game at Alabama ; however, he did not play. home.headline: Injury Report: Kirby Smart is Right to be Concerned About "Banged Up" Georgia Football
home.blurb: UGA RB Chauncey Bowens, WR Isiah Canion and Auburn transfer and UGA DL Amaris Williams are all listed as “out” on Wednesday night’s SEC injury report that schools are mandated to complete by conference rule. Amaris Williams has been out for some time, and was never expected to play in this contest, but his status as well as that of Bowens and Canion backs up coach Kirby Smart’s comments after the 20-17 win over Alabama Saturday night. “We're a beat-up football team right now,” Smart said at Bryant-Denny Stadium . “We have guys out left and right, and to have both those backs out and Isiah (Canion) out at receiver - tough deal, but we responded.” One of those two backs that didn’t play Saturday night was not on the injury report Wednesday night, either. Nate Frazier has only played a handful of snaps since Georgia’s lopsided win at Arkansas . He was listed as questionable for two weeks, and played sparingly against Vanderbilt. There was some other news for the Dawgs in the injury report. Star DB KJ Bolden is listed as questionable for the game Satuday against the Tigers. The Bulldogs are starting to get thin in the secondary as well as fellow safety Tyriq Green is listed as out for the game. home.headline: Georgia football injury report: KJ Bolden downgraded heading into Auburn game
home.blurb: While offensive lineman Marcus Harrison was removed from the report, Georgia safety KJ Bolden was downgraded from questionable to doubtful. Defensive back Tyriq Green (ankle) — out Outside linebacker Amaris Williams (knee) — out Wide receiver Thomas Blackshear (shoulder) — out Wide receiver Isiah Canion (right leg) — out Running back Chauncey Bowens (lower leg) — out Safety KJ Bolden (right leg) — doubtful Other possibilities include Zion Branch, Ja’Marley Riddle and Blake Stewart. Green would also be worth monitoring but he is out once again after suffering an ankle injury against Western Kentucky. Nate Frazier is once again absent from the availability report for Georgia, indicating he’s able to play. That was the case last week, before Frazier was held out of Georgia’s win over Alabama. Dwight Phillips ran for 120 yards while Bo Walker added another 69 on the ground. But with Bowens and Dante Dowdell both out for Georgia, it will be worth monitoring if Frazier sees the field. Georgia is a nearly three-touchdown favorite against the visiting Auburn Tigers. The Bulldogs also have an off week coming out of this game. The SEC will put out another availability report on Friday, before providing a final update 90 minutes before kickoff. Bolden has been one of Georgia’s most important players this season. He has 22 tackles, 2 pass breakups, 2.0 tackles for loss and an interception. He led Georgia in snaps played against Alabama. In the event he doesn’t play , Georgia does have options in the secondary. The Bulldogs could slide Rasean Dinkins over and play he and Kyron Jones at safety. Doing so would allow Georgia to keep Khalil Barnes at the star position. The Clemson transfer has excelled in that role for Georgia this season. The Bulldogs have looked like a team that is in store for a long season with how the first six weeks have gone. If they are to accomplish all of their goals this season, it will need Bolden and Frazier healthy and contributing at the end of the season. Saturday’s game is set for a 3:30 p.m. ET start.

home.headline: Kirby Smart says Georgia is 'beat up.' Here's the latest on injuries
home.blurb: "We're a beat up football team right now, guys," coach Kirby Smart said after the 20-17 win over Alabama. "We've got guys out left and right." Canion was listed as questionable last week on the SEC Availability Report before being downgraded Friday to out. Blackshear is out with a broken collarbone, according to ABC on Saturday night's broadcast. The average return to play for contact sports for a broken collarbone is 8 to 12 weeks, according to an Instagram post by Dr. Mike Galbraith, a Texas-based sports medicine physician. Freshman Craig Dandridge played a season-high 55 snaps with Blackshear and Canion out. "We had to go all week kind of not knowing on Isiah," Smart said Monday. "How does it affect you? You talk to Mike (Bobo), you talk to the offensive staff, it's frustrating because you don't really know who's in and who's out. You're trying to make decisions. We thought Nate was going to be able to play. That was a surprise to us. Isiah, we knew it would be close, maybe or maybe not. It just makes it hard because you can't get enough reps for guys." The No. 1 Bulldogs are dealing with several notable injuries heading into a week seven game Saturday at home against Auburn. Georgia played its third straight game without Isiah Canion, the transfer wide receiver from Georgia Tech who Smart said Monday is dealing with "a lower extremity injury." The Bulldogs were also without wide receiver Thomas Blackshear, who was injured in the win over Vanderbilt on Oct. 3. Phillips rushed for a career-high 120 yards on 17 carries against Alabama with Frazier and Chauncey Bowens sidelined. Bowens leads the team in rushing touchdowns. He was not listed on the availability report all last week, but warmed up and did not play Saturday. ABC's Holly Rowe said he made a quick cutting move and needed attention from the training staff. Phillips was asked Monday if he had an idea that Frazier wouldn't be able to go or was surprised. "That's probably a Kirby Smart question," he said with a smile. On the "Third Saturday in October," Tennessee hosts Alabama at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., as the Volunteers look to win against their rival for the third time in five years. The Crimson Tide are 7.5-point road favorites, and my Alabama vs. Tennessee prediction and college football picks expect Kalen DeBoer to continue Nick Saban's tradition of blowing out the Vols. TOP PICK Who will win Alabama vs Tennessee: Alabama -7.5 If last week was any indicator, Tennessee has far more problems than Alabama , despite the Volunteers' win and the Crimson Tide's loss. In George MacIntyre's first start for Josh Heupel, he finished with just a 10.3 QBR in a seven-point win against Arkansas. He'll be starting again against Bama, which is why I like the Tide to cover -9.5 or better . Arkansas lost to its previous three Power Four opponents by an average of 29.3 points, including a 28-point defeat to Georgia — the same team Alabama lost to by just three on the road last week. Tennessee's offense won't be able to keep up with Alabama. Keelon Russell ranks third nationally in QBR (90.0) , and the Tide are top 20 in offensive success rate (50.1%). The Alabama vs. Tennessee rivalry history is full of winning streaks, and this could be the start of another. Alabama vs Tennessee Over/Under pick: Over 50.5 For this Over to hit (I'd take it at 51.5 or better ), Alabama will need to do the bulk of the scoring, and the Tide will push for 31+ points given Russell's recent play. The former five-star recruit has put up an 8 0.9+ QBR in four straight games while accounting for 14 TDs. His dual-threat ability has helped open up the run game, too, with Alabama ranking fourth nationally in rush success rate (53.3%) . That will force Jim Knowles' defense to stay honest instead of solely focusing on protecting the back end. Meanwhile, Tennessee should be able to put up 20+ points to help push the total Over. The Volunteers have one of the best run games in the country (No. 2 in EPA per rush), led by DeSean Bishop . Bishop ranks top 10 nationally in rushing yards after contact (465). Alabama vs Tennessee combo One word describes Tennessee's passing game: rocky. The Volunteers are 128th nationally in pass success rate (33.8) , and MacIntyre has a QBR of 24.7 this season. That won't cut it against an Alabama defense tied for the 14th-most sacks in the country (17). I'm expecting a fast start from Russell after last week's tough loss to Georgia, and once Bama takes the lead, Tennessee isn't equipped to come back with MacIntyre behind center. Alabama Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell (12) scrambles with the ball against the Georgia Bulldogs. David Leong-Imagn Images. Following their loss to Georgia a week ago, the Crimson Tide head to Knoxville looking to get back on track. In this classic SEC showdown, I've found a few player props worth dabbling in, including another big outing from Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell. Without further ado, here are my Alabama vs. Tennessee prop picks . Before you get too far, be sure to check out all of our college football picks for Week 7. Best Alabama vs Tennessee props Prop pick #1: Keelon Russell Over 240.5 Pass Yards (53.27%) Alabama star sophomore quarterback Keelon Russell should be amped up to bounce back after an underwhelming 16-for-30, 185-yard performance with just one touchdown in the Crimson Tide's loss to Georgia. That said, it came against arguably the best defense in the country. It was Russell's worst performance since throwing for just 188 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Week 2 against Kentucky. Over six games this season, Russell still averages more than this prop at 266.5 passing yards per game. He draws a Tennessee defense that has shut down quarterbacks all season, allowing just 185 passing yards per game. However, what elite quarterback have the Volunteers actually shut down? "Well, they held Arch Manning to just 201 yards." Oh, like that holds up in the year of our Lord 2026. Russell is far better than Manning and has faced far tougher competition this season than what this Volunteers pass defense has seen. Coming off a matchup against one of the country's best defenses, the sophomore should clear 240 passing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 250.5 passing yards. Prop pick #2: DeSean Bishop Over 89.5 Rush Yards (50.74%) With Tennessee's run-heavy offense averaging nearly 43 rushing attempts per game this season, I don't expect that approach to change on Saturday against a very talented Alabama run defense. Over their last three games against Texas, Auburn, and Arkansas, the Volunteers still average 38.33 attempts per game . Tennessee should lean on its leading rusher, DeSean Bishop , to move the ball downfield . Last week against Georgia, this Crimson Tide defense showed some flaws when junior running back Dwight Phillips Jr. rushed for 120 yards on just 17 carries . That's the same number of carries Bishop averages per game this season, and Alabama is coming off a game where it struggled to stop the run. Bishop is averaging 113 yards per game and more than six yards per carry this season. If he gets his usual workload, he should be in a great spot to record 90-plus rushing yards on Saturday. Take this up to 95+ yards. Prop pick #3: Keelon Russell Over 24.5 Rush Yards (53.49%) I gave out this same prop last week, so I'll start this one the same way: If you can secure Russell's longest rush over 15.5 yards , take it! Russell has surpassed that mark in every game this season. Plus, the longest rush prop eliminates the possibility of sacks taking away rushing yards, so if you can access it, take it Over his standard rushing yards prop at 25+. However, Russell has still rushed for Over 25 yards in four of his six games this season . The sophomore quarterback is averaging 7.66 rushing attempts per game, and with the Crimson Tide likely to be leading, as the spread indicates, they'll eventually want to chew some clock. That should give Russell plenty of chances to rack up yards on the ground. The last mobile quarterback Tennessee faced was Auburn's Byrum Brown, who averages 16.2 rushing attempts per game and racked up more than 107 rushing yards against the Volunteers. Russell just needs 25 and should have plenty of opportunities on Saturday. Take this up to 30+ rushing yards. picks.blurb: 3 predictions for Alabama vs. Tennessee in Top 15 rivalry showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Packers' Josh Jacobs will be eligible to play Week 7 TRENDING Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead 3 predictions for Alabama vs. Tennessee in Top 15 rivalry showdown Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads On Saturday afternoon, the Alabama Crimson Tide will travel for what is arguably their toughest road test yet, facing the Tennessee Volunteers in Knoxville. The latest chapter in the storied Third Saturday in October rivalry, Alabama has dropped their last two games played in Neyland Stadium, and will face yet another significant challenge Saturday afternoon. Tennessee sits at 5-1 overall (2-1 SEC), and are currently ranked as the nation's No. 14 team in the latest US LBM Coaches Poll . A matchup that is loaded with potential storylines , following is a look at three predictions for Saturday's showdown in Knoxville between the Crimson Tide and Volunteers. Alabama defense forces three Tennessee turnovers Oct 10, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide defensive back Bray Hubbard (18) celebrates his interception during the second quarter against the Georgia Bulldogs at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images According to ESPN's Pete Thamel , Alabama's defense will be facing George MacIntyre at quarterback for Tennessee on Saturday afternoon, a sophomore who will be making only his second-career start. MacIntyre, who had two picks a week ago against Arkansas, will be facing an Alabama defense that leads the SEC with nine interceptions this year, and I'll predict to add at-least two to that total Saturday afternoon, if not more. Noah Rogers has breakout performance Oct 3, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide wide receiver Noah Rogers (5) runs after a catch during the fourth quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Alabama wide receiver Noah Rogers has played in three games since returning from an offseason injury, but has yet to fully breakout for the Crimson Tide having made only three catches for 55 yards. With the Crimson Tide's leading receiver, Ryan Coleman-Williams, set to miss Saturday's game , Alabama will certainly need someone at the position to step up, and I'll say Rogers does exactly that with his best performance since arriving in Tuscaloosa. Alabama offensive line bounces back with big showing Oct 3, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Alabama Crimson Tide offensive lineman Jackson Lloyd (77) lines up during the fourth quarter against the Mississippi State Bulldogs at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Alabama's offensive line, which allowed four sacks a week ago against Georgia, faces a significant test in Knoxville this Saturday in a Tennessee defense that is currently leading the nation with 25 sacks on the season. Despite the unit facing an unknown surrounding the status of starting center Racin Delgatty, I'll still predict a bounce back from the Crimson Tide's offensive front in not only pass protection, but also helping pave the way for a big showing on the Alabama run game. Hill and Umeozulu are the second and third Wolf linebackers on Alabama's depth chart. DeBoer shared on Oct. 5 that Umeozulu will take "probably a couple more weeks," and Hill will "be back this season, but more than likely not this week." That said, Hill is probable on the initial availability report. away.headline: Ryan Coleman-Williams injury update: Did officials miss targeting on Alabama WR?
away.blurb: ESPN's Laura Rutledge had previously reported that Coleman-Williams was expected to return to the game with a lower-body injury. Rutledge continued her report that Coleman-Williams came out of the locker room at halftime and went to the medical tent before heading out to the stationary bicycle on the sidelines. Be sure to check out USA TODAY Sports' new College Football Unfiltered podcast , hosted by USA TODAY Sports columnist Blake Toppmeyer. You can stream on YouTube or download via Apple podcasts and Spotify . The 6-foot receiver sustained an apparent lower-body injury late in the second quarter of Alabama's game against the Bulldogs at Bryant-Denny Stadium in Tuscaloosa when he went up for a catch on a second-and-3 pass from Keelon Russell. The Crimson Tide star got another injury scare in the fourth quarter after he took a hit to the head from Georgia defender KJ Bolden. There was no targeting penalty called on Bolden by the officials. He was seen on ESPN's broadcast at the 5:25 mark of the quarter being taken to the Alabama locker room. Coleman-Williams finished the first half with two receptions for 33 yards on five targets before adding his third catch in the second half. His biggest play of the night came on Alabama's final drive of the first half, a 23-yard reception that moved the Crimson Tide into Georgia territory. Alabama capitalized on the opportunity, as EJ Crowell punched in a 1-yard rushing touchdown as time expired to end the half. Here's the latest on Coleman-Williams' injury: Ryan Coleman-Williams injury update Coleman-Williams sustained an apparent lower-body injury in the final seconds of the first half. He later returned after halftime, even catching a pass on an Alabama field goal drive. He does have a slightly noticeable limp as well. Here's a look at the play on which Coleman-Williams was injured in the first half: Later, Coleman-Williams took a hard hit to the helmet on a third-down catch attempt. Bolden hit the talented receiver in the head, though officials declined to call him for targeting. Coleman-Williams exited the game to head to the locker room for an evaluation, Rutledge reported. He left on his own power. What injury does Ryan Coleman-Williams have? Following Alabama's loss to Georgia, Kalen DeBoer told reporters that Coleman-Williams has a head injury. away.headline: Injury updates on three Alabama starters who left Georgia game
Alabama Head Coach Kalen DeBoer Shares Updates on Injured Tide Players Ahead of Tennessee Road Trip
away.blurb: "With Racin [Delgatty], just with his lower-leg injury, just continue to evaluate him and kind of see where he’s at in the days ahead. Obviously, he’ll be pretty sore, kind of working through things and limited, for sure, early in the week. Certainly get some reps with other guys, in particular, probably Mal Waldrep, Casey Poe, guys like that." "But I think going back to Ryan, I'm just gonna say this about all these guys that I mentioned, just Josh Ford last week, I mean, these guys go through things throughout the week that you don't see," DeBoer said. "And Ryan, in particular, has been doing that and leading the charge, not just with what he does to try to be out there on the football field for practice, but the energy and just trying to be an uplifting and uniting factor for not just the offense, but our football team. So, I know he was out there battling again on Saturday, giving everything he got, and he had until the very end.” Skip to main content Skip to site footer What's Hot: Breaking Benjamin at the Tuscaloosa Amphitheater Contests 2025 Big Ol' Buck Hunting Contest Get the App Download on Android TUSCALOOSA, Ala. -- Alabama lost three starters during its 20-17 loss to Georgia, with the Crimson Tide losing defensive lineman Terrance Green late in the first half, wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams on the final offensive drive, and center Racin Delgatty on the final drive. On Monday, Kalen DeBoer updated the statuses of all three of them, with Ryan Coleman-Williams likely to miss some time dealing with a couple of injuries. Here is what head coach Kalen DeBoer said about the three of them during his Monday media availability. "Ryan has a couple of things going on. Worked through an injury to his knee that's been kind of going on, and so we'll deal with that," DeBoer said. "Got the head issue as well. So, we’re gonna address that, even the lower-extremity there this week. Pretty good chance we wouldn’t have him here this weekend. I think he would be probably week-to-week after that." "And then Terrance [Green], just keep evaluating him. This is an injury that’s been going on for a couple weeks now. Just re-aggravated it, and it’s been limiting him in practice. And trying to get him to the game, he, I thought, made a great effort in trying to do that. Just, again, re-aggravated it." DeBoer also circled back on Ryan Coleman-Williams, Josh Ford, and the physicality and toughness that players like those two have shown this season. Offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb also said NC State transfer WR Noah Rogers is "pretty close" to 100% after his A-Day injury. Rogers played just one snap in the Tide's 20-17 loss to Georgia. No. 6 Alabama will travel to Neyland Stadium to take on the 14th-ranked Tennessee Volunteers on Saturday, October 17. Kickoff is scheduled for 2:30 p.m. CT on ABC. Whoever wins this game will greatly increase their chances of making the College Football Playoff and will also keep their team alive to make the SEC Championship game . This coming Saturday Josh Heupe l and all of Tennessee faithful are hoping that it will be 3 wins in their last 3 tries at home. Coleman-Williams didn't return to the game after that hit. The Tennessee Vols will host the Alabama Crimson Tide next weekend in Knoxville in a game that's very important for both teams. Tennessee has won the last two matchups in Knoxville against Alabama. Alabama has a big injury concern for the Tennessee game Coleman-Williams suffered multiple injuries in Alabama's loss to Georgia. The junior wide receiver left the game with a knee injury but eventually returned. The bigger concern is the head injury that Coleman-Williams suffered later in the game. Alabama head coach Kalen DeBoer confirmed after the game that Coleman-Williams is dealing with a head injury. Reading between the lines, it's fair to assume that this is a concussion protocol situation. So again, we'll see what information is released this week on the talented wide receiver, but his status for the Tennessee game, at least at this point, is suddenly in doubt. Coleman-Williams had been struggling with drops early in the season (an issue that carried over from last year), but he'd been playing well as of late. Not having him on the field would certainly be a big loss for the Crimson Tide. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports.
