After the Tennessee football team benched Faizon Brandon during Oct. 3's 24-14 win over Auburn, he sustained an injury that has been given a key update ahead of Saturday's contest. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brandon had started the first five games for the Volunteers, but suffered a shoulder injury on Sept. 26 in the 20-17 loss to Texas, and tried to play through the issue against Auburn, but the team put in George MacIntyre instead. Head coach Josh Heupel would even give MacIntyre the nod for last Saturday's 24-17 win over Arkansas, as he would talk about the plan for the Crimson Tide. More on the quarterback situation with the Tennessee football team Per On3 Sports, MacIntyre and Brandon would take reps during Tuesday's practice , though the expectation stands that the latter will be on the "initial SEC injury report as he continues to work through his shoulder injury." Looking at how the freshman in MacIntyre played on Saturday, he threw for 247 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions, as Heupel said he was "decisive." "I thought he was decisive with the football," Heupel said Monday. "He was going to the right spot and made some plays. … Collectively as a group we got to do a better job of taking care of the football." At any rate, it remains to be seen what Heupel and the Tennessee football team do with the quarterback situation with Brandon and MacIntyre for Saturday's game against Alabama. Both squads enter with one loss and need a win this weekend to maintain a reasonable path to the College Football Playoffs. However, alongside the high-stakes of the matchup are the storylines revolving around each team’s roster. Rebels’ star running back Kewan Lacy will be facing his former team for the first time since leaving Missouri, following his true freshman season in 2024. Meanwhile, former Ole Miss starters Austin Simmons, Cayden Lee and Chris Graves Jr. all return to Oxford for the first time since they entered the transfer portal, following the Rebels’ deep run through last year’s playoffs. Saturday’s kickoff between the Rebels and Tigers is set for 2:30 p.m. CT on the SEC Network. Ole Miss entered the week as six-point home favorites. Ahead of the Rebels' latest pressure-filled matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis Welcome to the gauntlet that is the College Football Playoffs….or at least the very real warmup version of it. The loser of this weekend’s game in Oxford isn’t mathematically out of the 12-team race, but it’s going to be a loss that will be immensely hard to overcome looking at Ole Miss’ and Missouri’s schedule. As far as the actual matchup is concerned, going into the game, Missouri has played better on the defensive side of the ball and matches the Rebels’ offensive firepower with Austin Simmons and Jamal Roberts leading the way. The Tigers’ rush attack could have the ability to give the Rebels a long afternoon, and we’ll really find out if Ole Miss improved enough from its nightmare performance defending the run against Florida. Ole Miss doesn’t have to completely shut down Mizzou’s ground game, it more than likely won’t, but if it can limit Roberts and the rest of the production in the backfield, the Rebels should give themselves a real chance at picking up a critical win. In my mind, that’s going to be the key to victory for Ole Miss. I believe this game will come down to the final few possessions and whichever offense has the ball last in that scenario. Given the large sample size we’ve seen of Trinidad Chambliss in those types of situations, I have a hard time picking against those results. Ole Miss 34, Missouri 31 Matt Galatzan All of the talk is going to be about the return of Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee to Oxford, and Kewan Lacy facing off against his former team. However, there needs to be more talk about Missouri's defense, or more specifically, its pass rush. The Tigers have 18 sacks this year, which is tied with Texas for third in the SEC behind LSU and Tennessee. Meanwhile, the Rebels are No. 1 in the SEC in sacks allowed with just five. If the Rebels can protect Trinidad Chambliss and slow down a balanced Missouri offense, they will be in good shape. I think they do both just enough to get the win. Ole Miss 30, Missouri 27 I think Ole Miss will take home a hard-fought victory against former Rebels’ quarterback Austin Simmons, wide receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. and the rest of the Missouri Tigers. Simmons, Lee and running back Jamal Roberts are likely to give head coach Pete Golding and his defense trouble, leading to a “bend-don’t-break” type of performance, following a bounce-back game against Vanderbilt for the Rebels’ defense. However, I’m comfortable predicting Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, wide receiver Deuce Alexander and running back Kewan Lacy to outplay Simmons, Lee and Roberts and give the Rebels a high-scoring ranked win in Ole Miss’ homecoming game. Ole Miss 38, Missouri 31 Zion Trammell Ole Miss and Missouri feature star-studded quarterbacks in Trinidad Chambliss and Austin Simmons. This has the makings of a high-scoring affair, so whichever quarterback can protect the ball better could decide the outcome. I think Chambliss and Kewan Lacy play their best games of the year, and Ole Miss gets by with a win. Ole Miss 31, Missouri 28 Cooper Ferguson Back in the Vaught, I want to see a great response to the blowout victory in Nashville. All will go well if Trinidad Chambliss plays as he has so far. After a second-half respite in the Vanderbilt game, Kewan Lacy is primed for a breakout game in the 2026 campaign. I fear the talent and connection between Austin Simmons and Cayden Lee, but I do not see the Rebels dropping a game at VHS this season. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:27 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 13 Missouri travels to No. 9 Ole Miss for a massive SEC showdown. Can the Tigers pull off another upset, or will the Rebels defend Oxford? Two of the SEC's most intriguing teams are set to collide Saturday afternoon as No. 13 Missouri (5-1) travels to Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss (4-1). Both programs are coming off dominant victories. Missouri dismantled Texas A&M 27-6, while Ole Miss embarrassed Vanderbilt 52-17. With both teams sitting at 2-1 in conference play, Saturday's matchup could have major implications for the SEC Championship race and College Football Playoff. Missouri: The Tigers Are Legitimate Contenders Eli Drinkwitz has Missouri playing some outstanding football, particularly on defense. The Tigers are allowing just 17.7 points per game and rank eighth nationally in rushing defense, surrendering approximately 78 yards per contest. Offensively, former Ole Miss quarterback Austin Simmons has thrown for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns, and just one interception. Now, he gets an opportunity to prove himself against his former program. But Missouri's biggest weapon has been running back Jamal Roberts. Roberts has rushed for 828 yards and eight touchdowns, including consecutive 200-yard performances. Against an Ole Miss defense allowing 176.4 rushing yards per game, he could be in for another massive afternoon. Former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee has also been outstanding, recording 42 receptions for 616 yards and five touchdowns. If Missouri establishes its rushing attack early, the Tigers could control this game. Ole Miss: Can Trinidad Chambliss Carry the Rebels? Pete Golding has Ole Miss back in the national conversation following last season's historic playoff run. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss continues to be one of the most exciting players in college football, throwing for 1,435 yards and 11 touchdowns through five games. Wide receiver Deuce Alexander has emerged as his favorite target, recording 32 receptions for 503 yards and five touchdowns. The Rebels are averaging 38.8 points and nearly 434 yards per game, but their defense remains a major concern. Ole Miss is allowing 28 points per game, including an embarrassing 52-point performance against Florida earlier this season. And facing Missouri's balanced offense certainly won't make things easier. However, the Rebels have been outstanding at home, winning all three of their games in Oxford this season. How Each Team Wins Missouri must establish Roberts early and force Ole Miss into a physical, defensive battle. If the Tigers can dominate time of possession and limit explosive plays from Chambliss, they have an excellent opportunity to leave Oxford with a victory. For Ole Miss, everything starts with its passing attack. Missouri's defense has been elite against the run, meaning Chambliss will likely need to carry the offense. The Rebels must also force Simmons into mistakes and prevent Roberts from consistently reaching the second level. This matchup has all the ingredients for one of the best SEC games of the weekend. Missouri's rushing attack should give the Rebels serious problems, and I expect Roberts to surpass 100 yards once again. However, I trust Chambliss and the Ole Miss offense to deliver when it matters most. The Rebels' explosive passing attack, combined with a sold-out Vaught-Hemingway Stadium, should be enough to overcome Missouri's physicality. Expect a back-and-forth contest that comes down to the final minutes, with Chambliss engineering a late scoring drive to secure the victory. (5-1) headed to Oxford, MS for a battle with the #9 Ole Miss Rebels (4-1). Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 last week following the bye week and couldn’t have looked more crisp. Missouri on the other hand smoldered Texas A&M 27-6 and ran for more yards (247) than the Aggies had as an offense (216). Missouri is 7-1 all-time against Ole Miss as the last meeting was in 2019. Ole Miss’ lone win in the series came in 1974, 10-0! We can surely expect more than 10 points in this game as both offenses looked good last week. Missouri has ran for 467 yards and five touchdowns over the last two weeks with Jamal Roberts totaling 433 of those yards and all five scores. Ahmad Hardy has not returned to practice, so it’s been an opportunistic year for Roberts. This game is also a headliner quarterback Austin Simmons following his transfer from Ole Miss. Simmons has been fantastic for Missouri. He has a 14:1 TD to INT ratio after tossing his first pick of the season last week, plus a 64.8 completion percentage and 1,474 yards. Simmons was injured at Ole Miss and never saw the field as a starter for the Rebels again. Simmons was replaced by Trinidad Chambliss and we all know how that turned out. If the season ended today, Ole Miss would more than likely be in the college football playoff. The Rebels outgained Vanderbilt in yards last week 409-343 and forced four turnovers. The Rebels defense had its best showing against a P4 opponent holding the Commodores to 2.8 yards per carry, four punts, and two turnover on downs. The offense received a boost with Kewan Lacy returning to the lineup. Lacy ran for 39 yards and a touchdown on seven carries in the first half as Pete Golding eased him back into action. The Rebels ran for 196 yards and three scores, while Trinidad Chambliss accounted for one of those on top of airing it out for three touchdowns and 213 yards. Ole Miss looked like a contender out of the bye week, but Missouri is a step up in completion and playing well with their 1-2 punch of Simmons and Roberts. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Missouri scored on five out of 10 drives starting from the second quarter and Jamal Roberts had back-to-back 200-yard rushing performances. Roberts is the hottest running back in the country right now with 211 and 222 rushing yards against Florida and Texas A&M, along with five touchdowns. Roberts has four games of 100-plus yards this season and scored in five out of six games. Missouri Player to Watch on Offense: QB Austin Simmons Austin Simmons is set for a revenge game against Ole Miss and the guy who replaced him; Trinidad Chambliss . This will be fun! Simmons has looked great for Missouri and threw a season-high 340 yards against Florida two weeks ago. Simmons has four multi-touchdown games and tossed three scores against Kansas and Mississippi State. He wasn’t asked to air it out early in the season, but over the past three games he’s averaged 32.3 pass attempts per game compared to 22.6 in the first three weeks. If Jamal Roberts can’t find running lanes, then Simmons will surely be dropping back 30-plus times and looking to take matters into his own hands late. Simmons has 11 rushing attempts on the season and hasn’t scored a touchdown on the ground yet. He’s a sneaky anytime touchdown bet. The Missouri Tigers Defense: Versus a DI opponent, Missouri allowed a season-low in yards last week to Texas A&M at 216. Only 27 of those yards came on the ground as the Aggies were held to 1.2 yards per carry and no touchdowns. Missouri picked off Marcel Reed twice and held him to 19-of-39 (48.7%). Missouri ranks tied for 13th nationally with 3.0 sacks per game and ranks tied for 9th with 18 sacks on the season. The Tigers grabbed three sacks last week are they’re coming into the week at 31.2% on third downs (26th). Missouri held Texas A&M to 4-of-18 last week on third downs (22.2%). Missouri will be bringing the pressure, but Chambliss thrives under duress. It should be a fun to watch the chess match between Missouri’s edge rushers and Chambliss. Missouri Player to Watch on Defense: EDGE Deaden Hopkins Deaden Hopkins has only played in four out of Missouri’s six games, but boy has he made his presence felt. Hopkins has at least a 0.5 sack in all four games, including Texas A&M last week. Hopkins had a career-high 3.5 sacks at Mississippi State after posting 1.5 sacks versus both Troy and Kansas, plus a forced fumble and recovery in both too. If you catch yourself going “who was that” or “that was close to being offsides"; it’s probably Hopkins off the ball you’re talking about. away.blurb: THURSDAY Ole Miss vs. Missouri Injury Report: Safety MJ Preston Upgraded to Probable, Former Rebel Cayden Lee Also Probable ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – Ole Miss safety MJ Preston has been upgraded from questionable to probable ahead of Saturday's game between No. 9 Ole Miss and No. 13 Missouri, according to the SEC's second availability report released at 7:10 p.m. CT Thursday. For Missouri, former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee was also upgraded from questionable to probable, and former Rebels quarterback Austin Simmons remains probable. The Rebels list nine players as out, while Missouri lists six out and two doubtful. Safety Edwin Joseph remains out after undergoing a tightrope procedure on his ankle . Ole Miss: Offensive lineman Enoch Wangoy (No. 77) moved from questionable to out. Safety MJ Preston (No. 19) was upgraded from questionable to probable. Tight end Hayden Bradley (No. 80) remains questionable. Missouri: Wide receiver Cayden Lee (No. 19) was upgraded from questionable to probable. Offensive lineman Khalief Canty Jr. (No. 58) moved from questionable to out. Linebacker Jeremiah Beasley (No. 6) and tight end Brett Norfleet (No. 87) moved from questionable to doubtful. Safety Santana Banner (No. 15), edge Darris Smith (No. 19), cornerback Cameron Keys (No. 20) and offensive lineman Cayden Green (No. 70) were upgraded from questionable to probable. Missouri wide receiver Shaun Terry II, who was questionable Wednesday, is no longer on the report. Six Tigers who were listed as probable Wednesday are also off the list: DaMarion Fowlkes, Nicholas Rodriguez, Kensley Louidor-Faustin, Langden Kitchen, Jayden McGregory and Jordon Harris. The only change to the Ole Miss out list is Wangoy, a transfer from Florida. Preston's upgrade gives the Rebels another option at safety with Joseph sidelined. The biggest news for the Tigers is Lee. He leads Missouri with 42 catches for 616 yards and five touchdowns, and the upgrade means Simmons is likely to have his top target available in Oxford. Running back Ahmad Hardy remains out. Missouri trended healthier on Thursday, and the Lee upgrade is the change that matters most for the Ole Miss secondary. With Joseph out, the Rebels will need Nick Cull at nickel and safeties Ladarian Clardy and MJ Preston ready to handle a passing game built around Simmons and Lee. Robert Woodyard Jr., Missouri's third-leading tackler with 44 stops and an interception, remains questionable and is the Tigers' most important name to watch on Friday's report. away.headline: Injury update: Will Mario Craver play today for Texas A&M against Missouri?
away.blurb: Texas A&M star receiver Mario Craver has been listed as questionable all week against the Missouri Tigers, as he continues to recover from some bangs and bruises he has sustained throughout the season thus far. With the release of this morning's SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report , that status appears to remain for Craver with kickoff now under an hour and a half away. Craver is listed as a game-time decision for the Aggies in this report, meaning that fans will be sweating his status heading right up into the game. Craver's skill set makes him one of the toughest matchups for A&M's opponents on the entire team, so having him ready and available for the Aggies is key in this matchup. There are some positive signs for Craver going into this game, though: he was spotted heading out to warm up against the Tigers, potentially signaling that he will be ready to go. Warmups are warmups, but if he was trending towards not playing, this would not be happening. This is a similar pattern, though, to what we saw against Arkansas last week. Craver was listed as questionable throughout the week and called a game time decision against the Hogs, but he eventually was ready to go and saw a good number of snaps in the first half. He didn't play much of the later part of the game, as it looked like he had tweaked something in the touches he did get. Maybe that was out of a sense of safety, though, as the Aggies had the game well in hand by halftime, and were much more committed to the run than they were the pass against the Hogs. He eventually left the game with an apparent injury , though he did return later on in the contest. There was a similar story the following week against LSU, however: he was targeted a lot earlier on in the game, but eventually had to leave with some sort of injury before returning. Especially with Terry Bussey out, though, Craver's availability is paramount. There was a good showing from TK Norman last week, who looks ready to step into an increased role, but there's a big difference between Arkansas at home and Missouri on the road. home.blurb: THURSDAY Ole Miss vs. Missouri Injury Report: Safety MJ Preston Upgraded to Probable, Former Rebel Cayden Lee Also Probable ‘I've got to go out there and earn it’: Hunter Elliott returns with something to prove as Ole Miss opens fall OXFORD, Miss. – Ole Miss safety MJ Preston has been upgraded from questionable to probable ahead of Saturday's game between No. 9 Ole Miss and No. 13 Missouri, according to the SEC's second availability report released at 7:10 p.m. CT Thursday. For Missouri, former Ole Miss wide receiver Cayden Lee was also upgraded from questionable to probable, and former Rebels quarterback Austin Simmons remains probable. The Rebels list nine players as out, while Missouri lists six out and two doubtful. Safety Edwin Joseph remains out after undergoing a tightrope procedure on his ankle . Ole Miss: Offensive lineman Enoch Wangoy (No. 77) moved from questionable to out. Safety MJ Preston (No. 19) was upgraded from questionable to probable. Tight end Hayden Bradley (No. 80) remains questionable. Missouri: Wide receiver Cayden Lee (No. 19) was upgraded from questionable to probable. Offensive lineman Khalief Canty Jr. (No. 58) moved from questionable to out. Linebacker Jeremiah Beasley (No. 6) and tight end Brett Norfleet (No. 87) moved from questionable to doubtful. Safety Santana Banner (No. 15), edge Darris Smith (No. 19), cornerback Cameron Keys (No. 20) and offensive lineman Cayden Green (No. 70) were upgraded from questionable to probable. Missouri wide receiver Shaun Terry II, who was questionable Wednesday, is no longer on the report. Six Tigers who were listed as probable Wednesday are also off the list: DaMarion Fowlkes, Nicholas Rodriguez, Kensley Louidor-Faustin, Langden Kitchen, Jayden McGregory and Jordon Harris. The only change to the Ole Miss out list is Wangoy, a transfer from Florida. Preston's upgrade gives the Rebels another option at safety with Joseph sidelined. The biggest news for the Tigers is Lee. He leads Missouri with 42 catches for 616 yards and five touchdowns, and the upgrade means Simmons is likely to have his top target available in Oxford. Running back Ahmad Hardy remains out. Missouri trended healthier on Thursday, and the Lee upgrade is the change that matters most for the Ole Miss secondary. With Joseph out, the Rebels will need Nick Cull at nickel and safeties Ladarian Clardy and MJ Preston ready to handle a passing game built around Simmons and Lee. Robert Woodyard Jr., Missouri's third-leading tackler with 44 stops and an interception, remains questionable and is the Tigers' most important name to watch on Friday's report. home.blurb: Joseph underwent ankle surgery to address the injury, Ole Miss on SI confirmed. There isn't a timetable for his return at this point but it almost certainly rules him out for the Mizzou game. The initial SEC injury report on Wednesday evening will shed light on his official status. As it turns out, it appears that second opinion resulted in the surgery. Joseph was in Birmingham, AL on Tuesday, potentially where he spoke with doctors. The Ole Miss Rebels are dealing with a notable injury in their secondary ahead of Saturday's SEC matchup with the Missouri Tigers in Oxford. Ole Miss safety Edwin Joseph suffered an ankle injuy in last week's blowout win over Vanderbilt. His status remained unclear in the days after the game. But now, there's serious doubt about his availability over the next few weeks. Edwin Joseph Posts Pictures After Surgery Joseph shared pictures on social media after surgery with two thumbs up. A transfer from Florida State, Joseph is in his first year with the Rebels, making it unfortunate to see him dealing with an injury that required midseason surgery. Through five games so far this season, Joseph has tallied 18 total tackles (11 solo) and one pass defended. The Ole Miss secondary has had its issues but Joseph has been one of the better players in the back end of Pete Golding's defense. Edwin Joseph Got Second Opinion on Ankle Injury Golding told reporters earlier this week that Joseph would be getting a second opinion on his ankle. "My only concern from Saturday, from an injury standpoint, would be Edwin," Golding said. "It is an ankle. Got diagnosed yesterday with an ankle sprain. We're going to get another opinion on that tomorrow. We'll manage it throughout the week." This is a breaking news article that will be updated accordingly. picks.blurb: 7 bold predictions for Miami's rivalry matchup against the Florida State Seminoles Skip to main content About Canes Football Canes Basketball FanSided NCAA Sites Hurricanes All-Time Football Lists Canes Football Recruiting Hurricanes All-Time Basketball Lists Miami Hurricanes Basketball Recruiting The Joe Gaither Show on CanesCentral Saturday's game at Hard Rock Stadium between the Miami Hurricanes and Florida State Seminoles will show two programs at opposite ends of the development process. Mario Cristobal has Miami sitting at 5-0 after a run to the CFP national championship game, and Mike Norvell is once again fighting for his job after a 3-3 start for Florida State. Here are seven bold predictions for the matchup. 1. Ashton Daniels finishes with fewer than 30 rushing yards Daniels enters Saturday with 323 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns, so holding him under 30 looks aggressive on the surface. But roughly 42% of those yards, and half of the touchdowns, came in one game, when he ran for 136 yards and five scores against Virginia. Alabama held him to seven net rushing yards on 13 attempts, and Louisville limited him to 45 yards on 13 attempts last week. Miami has also had some success against mobile quarterbacks this year. Wake Forest's Gio Lopez had rushed for 97 yards in his first two games before finishing with minus-8 yards against the Hurricanes (only 11 yards once three sacks are removed). Clemson's Tait Reynolds had 92 rushing yards in his previous three games before finishing at minus-22. Miami has allowed zero quarterback rushing touchdowns this season. The under-30 yards prediction can also be paired with Daniels not scoring a rushing touchdown. The Hurricanes have allowed only one rushing touchdown all year, from Clemson running back Gideon Davidson in the fourth quarter, and zero in the first half. 2. Florida State finishes below 100 rushing yards as a team Florida State has 1,123 rushing yards on the season and averages 187.2 per game, fourth in the ACC, so holding the Seminoles under 100 would be huge for the Hurricanes. But Miami has surrendered only 14 rushing first downs all season, so there is some merit to this one. Florida State averages 4.84 yards per rush overall but falls to 3.02 when the score is tied, 3.46 when trailing by 8-14 points and 2.11 when trailing by 15 or more. Its largest rushing totals have come disproportionately while playing from ahead. Miami's opponents have averaged 1.07 yards per carry in the second quarter and 0.86 in the third. On second downs the Hurricanes have allowed 10 yards on 33 rushing attempts, or 0.30 per carry. If Miami gets ahead, Florida State's best offensive weapon will fade. 3. Miami rushes for at least 250 yards Miami already averages 220.4 rushing yards and 6.16 yards per carry, ranking third in the ACC in rushing yardage. Florida State is 14th in the ACC in rushing defense, allowing 993 yards so far this season (4.60 per carry through six games). In matchups against FBS opponents, the Seminoles are allowing 6.67 yards per rush with a 50% rushing success rate. Louisville ran for 397 yards and six touchdowns on 43 carries last week, averaging 9.2 yards per attempt, with Isaac Brown accounting for 235 yards. Miami would not need anything close to that efficiency to reach 250. At its current 6.16 yards per carry, 41 rushing attempts would produce roughly 253 yards. A game in which Miami is favored by three touchdowns creates a second-half script that could push the Hurricanes past 40 attempts. 4. Miami sacks Ashton Daniels at least five times Florida State has allowed 16 sacks through six games, third-most in the ACC behind only Virginia (2.67 per game). Miami has generated 16 sacks in five games, with the totals rising from one against Stanford to two against Florida A&M, three against Wake Forest, four against Central Michigan and six against Clemson. The prediction should come true if Miami stops the run and forces Florida State into obvious passing situations. Daniels is completing 59.5% of his passes with eight touchdowns and seven interceptions, and he drops to 53.6% in second halves. When Florida State is trailing by 8-14 points, its team completion percentage falls to 37.5%. Five sacks is a large number, but Miami just recorded six against another mobile quarterback in Reynolds while Florida State ranks among the ACC leaders in sacks allowed. 5. Darian Mensah completes at least 80% of his passes An 80% completion prediction against Florida State sounds high, but Mensah is completing 84.2% of his passes for the season. He has finished at 85% or better in four of five games, with Clemson's 66.7% the only exception. His first-half passing numbers are 80-of-92, and he is 37-of-40 in first quarters. Florida State has been particularly vulnerable early through the air, with opponents completing 76.1% of first-quarter passes. Overall the Seminoles have allowed nine passing touchdowns against three interceptions and FBS opponents have averaged roughly 7.3 yards per dropback against Florida State. 6. Florida State does not score a rushing touchdown Florida State has 16 rushing touchdowns, 10 from Daniels, and 15 of them have come in the red zone. Miami has allowed one rushing touchdown on 116 carries, and inside the red zone, opponents have rushed 12 times for 14 yards (1.17 per carry) with one touchdown. Teams have reached Miami's red zone only eight times in five games. This one has potential to be spoiled in garbage time, but this is about being bold and Miami's run defense has been stout. 7. Miami wins by at least 28 points Miami is favored by 21.5 points, and their average victory margin is 39.8 points, the best in the country and the largest through five games in program history. Only Wake Forest has finished within 28 points. Last week the Seminoles led Louisville 14-0 before being outscored 44-6 the rest of the way. If Miami can do everything already mentioned, a final margin in the range of 49-10 makes sense. away.blurb: Players ruled out aren’t a surprise: Wide receiver Joshua Moore (Upper-body; Out for Season), running back CharMar ‘Marty’ Brown (Left knee; Out for Season), tight end Luka Gilbert (Undisclosed; Out for Season), cornerback Ja’Boree Antoine (Undisclosed), right guard Max Buchanan (Left knee), and cornerback Romanas “OJ” Frederique Jr. (Left shoulder). Redshirt junior cornerback Damari Brown is another big piece returning. He logged just six snaps against Clemson; limited with an undisclosed injury. The Hurricanes’ secondary has faced the most adversity to start the season, but sophomore Bryce Fitzgerald moving from safety to cornerback and others stepping up, most notably freshman safety/nickelback JJ Dunnigan, have kept them above water. Meanwhile, the Seminoles have ruled out the following: running back Samuel Singleton Jr., 2ide receiver Devin Carter, safety Karson Hobbs, cornerback Jamari Howard, linebacker Blake Nichelson, cornerback Jordan Crutchfield, linebacker Izayia Williams, and linebacker Daylen Green. Linebacker Noah LaVallee is listed as questionable. The freshman has only appeared in one game this season – against Central Arkansas. The former three-star recruit logged three total tackles, two solos and an assist, a tackle for loss, and two quarterback hits. Defensive tackle Darryll Desir, cornerback Zae Thomas, and left guard/center Paul Bowling are listed as probable. LSU might have the best mix of talent, and it certainly has the highest-profile head coach, but it has two losses, and one of them was last week in a 35-34 overtime thriller to Kentucky. It's just assumed that Texas will find its way into the College Football Playoff, and maybe get to the SEC Championship first. But it just lost to an Oklahoma team that pulled off an all-time found-a-way 27-24 win in the Red River Rivalry. The Sooners only have one SEC loss – 41-13 to Georgia – but all of a sudden, the second half of the schedule doesn't seem that bad. Kentucky, because it's in the first year of the Will Stein era, and Oklahoma, because it beat Texas – both programs are in a good place. But the winner of this will still be alive in the SEC, and the other almost certainly won't. Kentucky vs Oklahoma: Quick Hits Oklahoma goes on the road for two of the next three weeks, traveling to Mississippi State, hosting South Carolina, and going to Florida. It's a key stretch for Kentucky with Vanderbilt at home next, followed by a date at Tennessee. The two programs have only met three times. Oklahoma won 29-8 in 1982 and 29-7 in 1980, but Bear Bryant's Kentucky won the 1951 Sugar Bowl. Start here – it's just not screwing up. UK turned it over three times in the loss to Alabama, twice in a win over South Alabama, and that's it. No turnovers on the road at Texas A&M and South Carolina, and none last week against LSU. And then there are the penalties – there aren't any. Kentucky is No. 1 in the SEC in fewest penalties and fewest penalty yards, and that matters. The lack of turnovers matters. It all matters, because Oklahoma probably can't pull this off without the Wildcats royally screwing up like Texas did last week. Why Oklahoma Will Win Kentucky needs its running game to rock, and that's going to be a problem. Georgia was able to power away on Oklahoma with a few big runs in the blowout win, but that's been about it. Michigan tried to run a lot, and it did just enough to get by, but it was a struggle. Texas wasn't exactly creative in the way it tried to run, and it got stuffed way too often. The Sooners are 3-0 when they don't allow a touchdown run, and 0-2 when they do. And … Kentucky vs Oklahoma Prediction, Betting Lines Kentucky's only loss came in the one game (Alabama) it failed to hit 100 yards rushing and didn't score a touchdown on the ground. Oklahoma will hold up defensively in a low-scoring game that comes down to a few key late stops, but this won't be easy for a team that failed to hit 300 yards of total offense against anyone but UTEP. Kentucky is 135th in the nation in third down conversions. Oklahoma is third in the nation in third down stops. And that's the ball game. picks.headline: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling
picks.blurb: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Packers' Josh Jacobs will be eligible to play Week 7 TRENDING Fantasy Basketball Sign Up Brewers sweep Dodgers Ryan Fitzpatrick rips Bo Nix How WNBA Finals will be won Guardians take 2-1 ALCS lead Story by Wildcats Wire Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 4:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels down to Norman to face the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, and both of these teams have plenty of momentum coming into this matchup. Arguably no team in the country has more momentum on their side than the Wildcats right now, coming off back-to-back walk off two-point conversions for the win in overtime. However, Oklahoma came off of their bye week and got a massive win over Texas in the Red River Rivalry game. With that being said, do not let the final score fool you, Oklahoma is still really struggling on offense. Oklahoma's offense will be the worst unit on the field this Saturday, and despite a big 27-24 win over Texas, the issues have not been fixed. The Sooners have scored just six offensive touchdowns since week two. They have only scored over 20 points twice this season, this was week one against UTEP and against Texas where they needed a blocked punt for a touchdown and a pick six to do so. This is a night game in Norman and will present a lot of adversity for Kentucky. The matchup to watch is the Kentucky offense versus the Oklahoma defense, but we will get into that side later. Basically every single offensive metric that you look at to determine offensive success, the Sooners rank bottom five in the SEC. Oklahoma ranks dead last in the conference in all of these statistics: Success rate, Rush SR%, EPA per rush, Explosive play rate and 1D+TD%. They also rank bottom five in the SEC in these statistics: EPA per play, EPA per dropback, Pass SR%, 3rd Down conversion rate, Early Down conversion rate and yards per play. This might be the worst offense Kentucky faces this season unless they can turn things around quickly. Oklahoma ranks first in the SEC in three-and-out rate and negative play percentage. The Sooners have the worst yards per carry average in the FBS. This is a stark contrast because Kentucky's defense ranks top five in the SEC in explosive % allowed and negative % forced. Kentucky's defense has excelled at three things this season: forcing turnovers, forcing negative plays and limiting explosives. This Oklahoma offense has struggled, but they do have some playmakers. The number one guy that should scare you, ironically, is number one Isaiah Sategna. Sategna is a dynamic receiver who is the one guy that can consistently create separation and he is dangerous with the football in his hands. Kentucky has to know where Sategna is on every snap because he is lightning in a bottle when he gets his hands on the football. John Mateer is a reckless but talented quarterback, he made the best throw of his season against Texas to set up the Sooners for the game winning field goal. Mateer threw a perfect back shoulder to Sategna from the far hash. Mateer has arm talent and is a dangerous runner, he immediately looks to run when a pass play breaks down. However, Mateer is extremely turnover prone, even moreso than LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt. Kentucky forced two turnovers on Leavitt, and they need to repeat that on Saturday. They have done a great job of forcing turnovers all season, they did it against Keelon Russell, Marcel Reed, LaNorris Sellers and Leavitt. This defensive line has to get pressure on Mateer to force him to play recklessly. The Wildcats have struggled with scrambling quarterbacks this season, but they were better last week against Leavitt--same thing applies this week with Mateer. Oklahoma as we stated, averages the fewest yards per carry in all of FBS. This is a game where Kentucky should be able to make Oklahoma one dimensional, which is a massive advantage for the Wildcats. The defense has to make Mateer uncomfortable in the pocket and they will have a great chance to win this football game. Kentucky's defense has the opportunity to have their best performance of the season this Saturday. By Cory Nightingale Published: Oct 15, 2026 · 5:07 PM EDT The Inside College Football crew gave its pick earlier this week for the huge SEC matchup on Saturday in Norman between No. 15 Kentucky and Oklahoma. The Wildcats are the ranked team among the 2 teams, coming in at No. 15, but the Sooners have their own momentum going despite being unranked after last week's stunning victory over then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. That means we have 2 teams who'll be coming into the Week 7 primetime clash with some serious good feeling. No. 15 Kentucky is 5-1 overall and on a 4-game winning streak, capped by back-to-back overtime wins over South Carolina and LSU by the exact same 35-34 score. The Cats are 3-1 in the SEC, with their lone conference setback against Alabama in Week 2 feeling like a long time ago. Then there is Oklahoma, which suffered through a 2-2 September that took it from the AP rankings straight out of those rankings. But the win over Texas last week at the Cotton Bowl could be a season saver, with the 3-2 Sooners trying to gain momentum through the middle of the season. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Oklahoma game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue October 16, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Following an emotional win vs. No. 10 LSU, Kentucky heads to Oklahoma to face a Sooners team that just beat No. 1 Texas. What a wild Saturday it was for the Kentucky Football team. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky’s offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners’ other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners’ stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer’s primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. Kentucky will need to account for all three playmakers while also limiting the Sooners’ running game, which features Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton Jr. Game: Kentucky Football vs. Oklahoma Sooners Location: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium — Norman, Oklahoma Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET TV Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog . ESPN gives Kentucky a 32.1% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 5-1 under first-year head coach Will Stein after a huge upset over LSU, while Oklahoma is coming off a rivalry win over Texas. Both teams could experience an emotional hangover after their big victories, but I believe Kentucky can overcome that challenge and earn another road win. Despite concerns about linebacker injuries, the Wildcats have a chance to improve to 6-1, become bowl-eligible, and remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. picks.headline: How No. 15 Kentucky football & Oklahoma match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Having led Kentucky to back-to-back 35-34 overtime wins, Kenny Minchey is proving himself a cool customer under game-deciding stress. Two weeks ago at South Carolina, Minchey had running back CJ Baxter make a pre-snap shift so he could pick up an otherwise-free edge rusher. As the block was achieved, Minchey threw the game-winning two-point-conversion pass. Last week, Minchey realized the LSU defense had a Grand Canyon-sized hole in the middle of its formation. On a called pass play, the Hendersonville, Tennessee, product instead ran right through that hole for the game-winning two-point-conversion run. On the season, the 6-foot-2, 211-pound Minchey is completing 67.4% of his passes and has thrown for 1,394 yards with 11 touchdown throws vs. one interception. • Oklahoma’s John Mateer began the season on the outskirts of the Heisman Trophy discussion but has so far had a rough go in 2026. Ball security has been a problem for the 6-1, 224-pound Mateer. He threw a crucial interception late in Oklahoma’s 17-10 loss at Michigan in Week 2. He also turned the ball over three times in the first half at Georgia on Sept. 26, helping the Bulldogs open a 28-0 halftime lead en route to a 41-13 win. In Oklahoma’s 27-24 upset of then-No. 1 Texas last week, however, Mateer completed 18 of 26 passes for 155 yards with no interceptions. Mateer has not been as effective a rusher so far in 2026 as he has been in past seasons. Through five games, Mateer has a net-70 yards rushing. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • Kentucky’s CJ Baxter ripped off a 77-yard run on UK’s first play from scrimmage in last week’s win over LSU. The 6-1, 230-pound product of Boynton Beach, Florida, finished with 123 rushing yards on 19 carries against the Tigers. A transfer from Texas, Baxter is fifth in the SEC in rushing with 484 yards. Third-year player Jason Patterson has carried only seven times combined in the past two games after suffering an apparent injury at South Carolina. A 5-10, 204-pound product of Sneads, Florida, Patterson had been one of UK’s breakout players over the season’s first four games. • Oklahoma’s ground game has, so far, been mostly stalled. The Sooners are last in the SEC in rushing, averaging only 95.8 yards a game. Lloyd Avant Jr ., a transfer from Colorado State who began his college career at Tulsa, leads the Sooners in rushing with 239 yards and two touchdowns on 52 carries (an average of 4.5 yards a rush). Avant, however, had a strong showing in the win over Texas, rushing 10 times for 72 yards and a touchdown. Wide receivers • Kentucky true freshman Kenny Darby was named SEC Freshman of the Week for the second straight week after catching four passes for 79 yards, including two crucial receptions late in the game, in the win over LSU. On the season, Darby, a 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, is eighth in the SEC in receptions (29) and ninth in receiving yards (401). Ja’Kayden Ferguson had caught only three total passes in UK’s first five games, but the 6-2, 184-pound, second-year player made three key receptions in the win over LSU. “He made some unbelievable plays,” Will Stein said of Ferguson. “... He blocked hard. He played hard. He’s got a lot of talent, a lot of upside.” • Isaiah Sategna III has been Oklahoma’s most effective offensive skill player so far in 2026. The 5-10, 185-pound senior from Austin, Texas, has 25 catches for 331 yards and two touchdowns. Sategna caught five passes for 64 yards in the win over Texas. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez made a team-high six catches for 25 yards vs. LSU. A 6-4, 249-pound junior from Covington Catholic, Rodriguez is second on the UK team in receptions (28) and receiving yards (219). Henry Boyer had a quiet showing vs. LSU with one catch for four yards. The 6-6, 270-pound transfer from Illinois has only nine catches on the season, but those receptions have yielded 120 receiving yards and three touchdowns. • Oklahoma’s Rocky Beers is, like UK’s Rodriguez, one of the best pass-catching tight ends in the SEC. A 6-5, 240-pound senior from Littleton, Colorado, Beers has 22 receptions for 284 yards and two touchdowns. Beers had four catches for 29 yards vs. Texas. Hayden Hansen caught 30 passes for 254 yards and two TDs last season while playing for Florida. So far this season, the 6-8, 270-pound Hansen has five catches for 74 yards and a TD. Advantage : Even Offensive line • After having a rough go against Alabama in Week 2, Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood has consistently been playing solid football. “Malachi is a really-good football player,” Will Stein said. “The guy is 6-8, 330 pounds. He is gonna be, probably, a top three-round NFL draft pick in the next couple years. “ • The Oklahoma offensive front has been much-criticized amidst the Sooners’ offensive struggles, but the unit showed some signs of hope in the second half vs. Texas. Freshman Noah Best has emerged as the jack-of-all-trades on the OU offensive line, already logging starts this season at center and both guard positions. Defensive line • Kentucky nose guard Jamarrion Harkless was one of the unsung heroes of the win over LSU. The 6-3, 346-pound alumnus of Frederick Douglass High School made three tackles, 1.5 sacks, forced a fumble and had a quarterback hurry against Lane Kiffin’s Tigers. “I told (Harkless) ‘That’s how you have to play for us to be successful on defense, game in, game out,’” Will Stein said. • Oklahoma defensive tackle David Stone is an interior force. The 6-3, 312-pound junior from Del City, Oklahoma, made five tackles in the win over Texas. On the season, Stone has 19 tackles, two tackles for loss and half a sack. Advantage : Oklahoma • Due to injuries, Kentucky starting linebackers Grant Godfrey and Bo Barnes had to be iron men vs. LSU. WLB Barnes made 12 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss, while MLB Godfrey made 10 stops vs. the Tigers. • Oklahoma MLB Owen Heinecke leads the Sooners in tackles (36), is tied for the team lead in quarterback hurries (two) and is second in tackles for loss (4.5). A 6-1, 226-pound fifth-year player from Tulsa, Heinecke made nine tackles vs. Texas. Defensive backs • Kentucky senior strong safety Ty Bryant made six tackles and intercepted a pass vs. LSU. For the 6-foot, 196-pound Bryant, a product of Frederick Douglass High School, it was his sixth career pick. Cornerback Terhyon Nichols made seven tackles and successfully defended a pass vs. LSU. • Oklahoma strong safety Peyton Bowen returned an interception of Texas quarterback Arch Manning 42 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter last week. A 6-foot, 200-pound product of Corinth, Texas, Bowen has made 24 tackles on the season, leads the Sooners in pass breakups with four and also has a forced fumble and a sack. Special teams • Kentucky punt returner Brock Coffman brought an LSU kick back 55 yards for a touchdown last week. Place-kicker Adam Zouagui entered last week’s game 6 of 7 on field-goal attempts but went only 2 of 4 vs. LSU. However, after missing two makeable field goals in the fourth quarter last week, Zouagui came back to hit a 33-yard field goal with 12 seconds left in the contest to tie the game at 27 and force overtime. After Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara punted in UK’s first five games, the Cats turned to former starter Wilson Berry vs. LSU. On three punts, Berry averaged 40.1 yards and pinned LSU inside its 20-yard line once. • Oklahoma’s special teams are elite. Danny Okoye blocked a Texas punt last week that Dakoda Fields recovered in the Longhorns’ end zone for a touchdown. Isaiah Sategna III is second in the SEC in punt returning, averaging 18.57 yards a return. He had an 88-yard punt-return touchdown in the season opener vs. UTEP. Punter Jacob Ulrich is averaging 44.31 yards on 16 kicks and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line three times. Place-kicker Tate Sandell kicked a 47-yard field goal on the game’s final play to beat Texas last week. On the season, Sandell is 5 of 8 on field goals with a long make of 53 yards (which also came against Texas). picks.blurb: Oklahoma Sooners vs. Kentucky Wildcats final score predictions: Can the Sooners get back in the CFP discussion with a win? Skip to content NFL Close Menu All NFL Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks College Football Close Menu All College Football Alabama Crimson Tide Auburn Tigers Florida Gators Georgia Bulldogs Miami Hurricanes Michigan Wolverines Notre Dame Fighting Irish Ohio State Buckeyes Oklahoma Sooners Ole Miss Rebels Penn State Nittany Lions Tennessee Volunteers Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Draft Simulator Trade Simulator Toggle Mobile Navigation Home College Football The Oklahoma Sooners will host a strong Kentucky Wildcats team on Saturday night. The Oklahoma Sooners are coming off of a huge win over the Texas Longhorns at the Cotton Bowl in the Red River Rivalry. The Kentucky Wildcats are coming off a huge overtime win over LSU. Both teams are on a high but are looking to improve their records on Saturday night. So, does the team in Kentucky that's maybe at its best as a program get the win? Or does Oklahoma get another ranked win and get back into the College Football Playoff conversation? Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee : Oklahoma 20, Kentucky 17 This feels almost like the clock striking midnight for Kentucky here, as much as it does for me, who's lived the last two weeks dangerously. Both teams are coming in off super highs from last week. Oklahoma clipped Texas 27-24 on a walk-off field goal. Kentucky walked off LSU 35-34 in overtime, their second straight walk-off overtime win, going for two and getting it on the final play. Honestly, in a vacuum, I trust Kentucky QB Kenny Minchey more than I trust OU's John Mateer. But Minchey is going up against a very good Oklahoma defense, while Mateer has a more navigable task when he has the ball. I still don't see points a plenty here, but Oklahoma forces a key turnover late, and that's enough with the home crowd in Norman to get a close and resume-boosting win at the season's midpoint. Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame : Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 20 This could be one of the ugliest games on the schedule, with both teams struggling to find much offensive consistency. Oklahoma will have chances to pull away, but John Mateer’s chaotic style makes it hard to trust the Sooners to put together four clean quarters. Mateer can make spectacular plays, but mistakes and questionable decisions could give Kentucky the extra possessions it needs to hang around. Don't expect a shootout here. This game could come down to which team makes fewer costly mistakes in the fourth quarter. I'm buying a little bit of Kentucky magic in this one. Kenny Minchey comes through with a couple of clutch plays at the biggest moments, giving the Wildcats just enough offense to pull off a road upset. Kentucky might not look dominant, and it certainly won't be pretty, but this team finds a way to make things interesting when the game is on the line. Oklahoma has a chance to put the Wildcats away but can't quite finish the job, opening the door for Kentucky to steal a win in a close, low-scoring battle. Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida : Kentucky 21, Oklahoma 16 Will Stein has the Wildcats on a heater right now, and he's doing it with the two things you want in Kentucky's place: confidence and guts. He's won two games this season because the Wildcats went for two at the end, and that kind of belief in your team will go a long way in establishing a foundation for your program. Things are different for the Sooners, who are coming off of a fantastic win in Red River. Even so, John Mateer can't do much other than throw shock, and he did that brilliantly on the final drive against Texas. I don't think Mateer will change overnight, and the Wildcats will take advantage of him enough to win. Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama : Oklahoma 21, Kentucky 14 This game suddenly looks much better than it did a week ago after both Kentucky and Oklahoma pulled off massive upsets last weekend. Red River can always get wonky, but few expected OU to beat the number one team in the nation given how the offense has played. Will Stein's Wildcats have gone from quietly looking like a good football team to potentially being one of the conference's better teams after just one loss to Alabama and a last-minute OT win over LSU. The truth, however, is that OU may have found something more than just some Red River magic. This will be arguably the hardest test of the year for Kenny Minchey, and the battle of the brains between Brent Venables and Will Stein will be notable, but I think Oklahoma will get the job done. Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma : Oklahoma 21, Kentucky 17 The Oklahoma Sooners are almost ready to kick off their first SEC night game (excluding CFP games) since 2024. And this one should be big, with both teams riding an insane high after huge wins. The Kentucky Wildcats will give OU's defense fits. It will happen, and I know my score prediction probably doesn't show that, but I have OU getting a few takeaways in this one. Kentucky is going to do a bunch of pre-snap stuff that's going to confuse you. They are very good at that, but Brent Venables has his unit locked in right now. OU will win this game once again through the defense and special teams, with some little moments here and there from the offense. University of Oklahoma Sports Oklahoma, Kentucky release injury reports ahead of Saturday’s game Michael Fasusi and Eli Bowen are among six Oklahoma players listed as questionable ahead of Saturday’s matchup in Norman. Michael Fasusi and Eli Bowen are among six Oklahoma players listed as questionable ahead of Saturday’s matchup in Norman. The Sooners have five players listed as out, two doubtful, three questionable and two probable for the game. Oklahoma wide receiver Parker Livingstone and offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis are now listed as doubtful after appearing as questionable on Wednesday’s report. Linebacker Taylor Heim, wide receivers Trell Harris and defensive back Jacobe Johnson remain out, along with running back Xavier Robinson and tight end Trynae Washington. Defensive back Eli Bowen and offensive linemen Michael Fasusi, Fred Hinton and Heath Ozaeta are questionable. Running back Tory Blaylock and tight end Jack Van Dorselaer are probable. Kentucky has five players listed as out, four questionable and two probable. Defensive end Tyler Thomas is now out after being listed as doubtful Wednesday. Inside linebackers Antwan Smith and Tavion Wallace, along with defensive backs Jaden Smith and Grant Grayton, also remain out. Cornerback Eli Bowen is a key name to watch for the Sooners' defense. He was injured in practice on Thursday and missed the win over Texas. If he doesn't play Saturday night, Trystan Haynes would get his second consecutive start after playing well against the Longhorns . For the Kentucky Wildcats, one of the most important names to watch ahead of Saturday's primetime affair is running back C.J. Baxter. Baxter joined Kentucky via the transfer portal from Texas. He's run for 484 yards and eight touchdowns at 5.6 yards per carry this season. It would be a big blow to the Wildcats, but they have capable runners behind him on the depth chart in Jason Patterson (361 yards, 7.7 yards per carry) and former Sooner Jovantae Barnes (140 yards, 6.1 yards per carry). picks.headline: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction
picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! LOOKING FOR REVENGE? Dylan Raiola will have to earn the opportunity to face his former team in Nebraska. A two-year starter for the Cornhuskers, Raiola has faced external criticism for his decision to transfer to Oregon, but he maintains a strong relationship with Nebraska coach Matt Rhule and several of his former teammates. Raiola's performance against UCLA last week was one of the worst by an Oregon quarterback in recent memory: 6 of 19 passing, 43 yards and two interceptions. home.blurb: Moore returned to practice this week, but he remains in concussion protocol and was officially listed as out on Oregon’s availability report. The Ducks are taking a cautious approach to his recovery, with no timetable announced for his return. Moore returned to practice on Monday, October 5 , following Oregon’s bye week. His return was an encouraging development, but it did not mean he was ready to play. Lanning said the Ducks would continue to prioritize what was best for Moore as he worked through the recovery process. Moore remained in concussion protocol and was ruled out for the UCLA game on the conference’s availability report released Wednesday. The quarterback must complete the necessary steps in the concussion protocol before he can return to game action. Oregon has not announced a target date for his comeback. With Moore unavailable, Dylan Raiola is set to make his first start for Oregon . The former Nebraska quarterback replaced Moore against USC and helped the Ducks secure the victory, completing 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns . “He had an expectation when he stepped out there on the field and performed at a really, really high level, and everybody had confidence in him because they see him do it a lot in practice, ” Lanning said.
